Nuclear Theory [23]
☆ u3lib: An AI-Ready Computational Framework for U(3) Symmetry Algebra, Wigner Coupling, and Racah Recoupling Coefficients
Daniel Langr, Phong Dang, Tomas Dytrych, Michela Negro
u3lib is a C++ library for U(3)/SU(3) representation-theory calculations in nuclear structure and related applications. It evaluates Wigner coupling and Racah recoupling coefficients using the procedure proposed in 2024 by Dang et al., which avoids the binomial coefficients and alternating sums used in earlier formulations. The library also provides irreducible representations (irreps), dimensions, Casimir invariants, conjugation, and tensor-product decompositions with outer multiplicities. It supports the canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin basis and the physical SU(3) $\supset$ SO(3) basis, including inner multiplicities and the transformation between the two bases. Generator routines return matrix elements in the canonical basis and reduced matrix elements in the physical basis. Python bindings mirror the C++ API. Domain skills supplied with the repository allow an AI assistant with code-execution access to call these routines from natural-language requests.

☆ Probing the structure of the two proton Borromean nucleus $^{17}\rm{Ne}$ through inclusive breakup data
B. Pinheiro, M. Rodríguez-Gallardo, J. Lubian
The proton-rich nucleus $^{17}$Ne exhibits a Borromean structure, $^{15}$O+p+p, since both $^{16}$F and diproton systems are unbound. The low-energy spectrum of this nucleus consists of a series of resonances that remain poorly identified. In this work, a three-body model is used to describe the structure of $^{17}$Ne, with special attention to the emergence of resonant states. The four-body continuum-discretized coupled-channel (CDCC) formalism is used to study the reaction of $^{17}$Ne on a $^{208}$Pb target near the Coulomb barrier. Comparing the calculated elastic and breakup cross sections with the recently available experimental data~\cite{OVEJAS2023138007} provides an excellent framework for probing the resonant structure of this nucleus.
☆ Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
G. Hagen, T. Papenbrock
The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^π=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.

☆ The antibaryon-baryon interaction based on chiral EFT with a focus on $\bar pp$ and $\barΛΛ$ reactions
Qin-He Yang, Johann Haidenbauer, Ulf-G. Meißner
The antibaryon-baryon ($\bar BB$) interaction is reviewed in the context of the hyperon(Y)-production reactions $\bar NN\to\bar YY$ with special emphasis on the $\bar ΛΛ$ system. The experimental situation for $\bar BB\to\bar YY$ from threshold up to antiproton lab momenta of $2$ GeV/c is discussed and likewise past theoretical approaches and results. The formalism for a description of the $\bar BB$ interaction in terms of potentials derived within SU(3) chiral effective field theory (EFT) is outlined. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry on the $\bar BB$ interaction in the various reaction channels are discussed. As concrete application a new analysis of the reaction $\bar pp\to\bar ΛΛ$ is performed utilizing potentials for the $\bar NN$ and $\bar ΛΛ$ channels, and for the $\bar NN\to\barΛΛ$ transition, up to next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion, supplemented by a phenomenological part to account for annihilation processes. An excellent reproduction of data from the PS185 experiment at CERN up to momenta of $1.55$ GeV/c is achieved. When including higher-order contact terms in the analysis the range of agreement can be extended up to momenta around $1.65$ GeV/c, where a complete set of scattering observables is available. Predictions for $\barΛΛ$ scattering are provided and compared to results from the literature.

☆ Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
Gopal Mistry, Amaresh Jaiswal
We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

☆ Rigid triaxial roto-vibrator in a finite system
A. Leviatan
We investigate the emergence of rigid triaxiality in a finite system, within the framework of the interacting boson model of nuclei. Appropriate Hamiltonians for a maximally-triaxial rigid shape are constructed. Closed expressions for wave functions, energies and E2 rates for states of the ground band are derived. Classical and quantum analyses reveal that for a fixed Hamiltonian, the system evolves from a $γ$-soft SO(6) structure for small $N$, to a $γ$-rigid structure for large $N$. Attention is paid to symmetry and spectral properties of both rotational and vibrational states.

☆ Inclusive and diffractive D meson photoproduction in $pPb$ collisions at the LHC using Pythia8 framework
Victor P. Goncalves, Luana Santana, Wolfgang Schäfer
We present a systematic analysis of inclusive and diffractive $D$-meson photoproduction in $ep$ and ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions within the Pythia8 framework. Predictions obtained with different proton and Pomeron PDFs are compared with H1 measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^*$ photoproduction at HERA. We also present predictions for the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction at the LHC. Our analysis indicates that the diffractive contribution exceeds 15\% at low $p_T$ and forward rapidities, suggesting that diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction could be accessible in future LHC runs. In addition, measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions can help constrain the proton and Pomeron PDFs.

☆ Nucleon Short-Range Correlations and Supersoft Nuclear Symmetry Energy: Compatibility with Massive Neutron Stars and GW170817
Hai-Xiang Zhu, Bao-Jun Cai, Yu-Gang Ma
Massive neutron stars (NSs) require a sufficiently stiff core equation of state (EOS), while the relatively small tidal deformability inferred from GW170817 favors softer nuclear matter at intermediate densities. Given the importance of the nuclear symmetry energy in neutron-rich matter, an intriguing question arises: Can the symmetry energy become supersoft at high densities while remaining compatible with these seemingly competing constraints? Within the nonlinear Walecka framework, we demonstrate that nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs), manifested as a high-momentum tail (HMT) in the nucleon momentum distribution, can accommodate such behavior without introducing additional interaction parameters. We derive for the first time analytical expressions for the symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ for both free Fermi gas (FFG) and HMT momentum distributions. Using model parameter sets that reproduce empirical nuclear matter properties around saturation density, we find that SRC-HMT yields substantially more negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$ than the FFG case, allowing the symmetry energy to reach a maximum at low supra-saturation densities and subsequently decrease while the total pressure remains sufficient to support massive NSs. The resulting EOSs also predict smaller NS radii and tidal deformabilities consistent with GW170817. These results connect the microscopic nucleon momentum distribution with the density dependence of the symmetry energy and macroscopic NS properties.

☆ Light-particle emission in nucleon-induced fission of $^{235,238}$U at energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV
Fuchang Gu, Yingge Huang, Qiafeng Chen, Jun Su
Background: In nucleon-induced fission up to GeV energies, early nonequilibrium emission alters the residual nuclei before statistical evaporation and scission. The emitted light particles therefore probe each reaction stage while supplying needed nuclear data. Purpose: We study neutron and light charged-particle emission in $^{235,238}$U$(n,f)$ and $^{235,238}$U$(p,f)$ reactions at incident energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV. Methods: The reactions are simulated event by event by coupling the isospin-dependent quantum molecular dynamics model with the GEMINI++ statistical decay code. Results: The calculations follow the measured rise in average neutron multiplicity with incident energy, while yielding higher values above 100 MeV and in the proton-induced prescission component. Within the coupled calculations, the neutron multiplicity growth comes mainly from statistical evaporation before scission, whereas emission from the fission fragments changes weakly. Although the average preequilibrium neutron yield remains small, early emission spreads the residual nuclei across multiple elements and wide excitation energies. At high energies, protons are emitted predominantly before equilibration, directly reducing the charge retained by the residual nuclei. Conclusions: In the coupled calculations, statistical evaporation before scission governs the neutron multiplicity growth, whereas early nonequilibrium emission shapes the residual nuclei and dominates high-energy proton emission. These results provide a reference for modeling intermediate-energy fission, in which prescission emission changes the charge, mass, and excitation energy of the fissioning system.

☆ Particle-vibration coupling model with explicit doorway states based on the Skyrme density functional
W. L. Lv, Y. F. Niu, G. Colò
Modern $γ$-ray detectors can achieve energy resolutions of a few keV, motivating microscopic studies of strength fragmentation in nuclear excitation spectra. Particle-vibration coupling (PVC) describes the spreading of giant resonances, but conventional formulations based on an energy-dependent effective Hamiltonian in the 1 particle-1 hole (1p1h) space do not explicitly provide individual excited states and their wave functions. We develop a PVC model with explicit doorway states by directly diagonalising the PVC matrix in the space of 1p1h and 1p1h coupled to a phonon (1p1h$\otimesν$) configurations. Using the Skyrme energy density functional SkM*, we study the isovector giant dipole resonance (GDR) in $^{208}$Pb. The one-body transition densities show that the neutron and proton components of the dominant GDR states remain out of phase after including PVC, preserving their isovector character. Wave-function analysis reveals that the $2^+$ and $3^-$ phonons play a key role in GDR fragmentation. The fragmented states are dominated by 1p1h$\otimesν$ configurations, accounting for more than 80\% of the wave-function norm. Nevertheless, coherent contributions of 1p1h configurations preserve the collective character of the $E1$ transitions. Thus, PVC strongly modifies the microscopic structure and fragmentation of the GDR without changing its essential isovector collective character.

☆ Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
Tomoyuki Maruyama, A. Baha Balantekin, Myung-Ki Cheoun, Toshitaka Kajino, Eunseok Whang
We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

☆ Impact of Effective Nucleon Mass and Symmetry Energy on Nuclear Pasta Phases and the Unified Equation of State of Neutron Stars
Shuying Li, Hong Shen, Jinniu Hu
We investigate how the effective nucleon mass and symmetry energy affect pasta phase properties and the unified equation of state (EOS) of neutron stars. The nonuniform pasta structure is described within the self-consistent Thomas-Fermi approximation, while nucleonic interactions are treated in the relativistic mean-field framework with several typical parameter sets adopted. Our results indicate that the symmetry energy and its slope are crucial in determining the onset of pasta phases and their geometric configurations. In the high-density region where matter becomes uniform, the effective nucleon mass plays a dominant role. A larger effective nucleon mass tends to soften the EOS, which yields a smaller radius for a canonical $1.4 M_{\odot}$ neutron star and reduces the corresponding tidal deformability.

☆ Structure and Binding of the \texorpdfstring{$pnΩ^-$}{pnOmega} System with a Near-Unitary \texorpdfstring{$NΩ$}{NOmega} Interaction from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
Faisal Etminan
The binding and spatial structure of the \(pnΩ^-\) system are investigated in the \(I(J^P)=0(5/2^+)\) channel using the physical-point HAL QCD \(NΩ({}^{5}S_2)\) interaction. The pairwise Hamiltonian includes the spin-triplet \(pn\) interaction and the finite-size Coulomb attraction in the \(pΩ^-\) pair. The three-body Schrödinger equation is solved with the Gaussian Expansion Method (GEM), including all three Jacobi rearrangement configurations. For the central HAL QCD potential at \(t/a=14\), the calculated three-body binding energy is \(18.63\) MeV, corresponding to a separation energy of \(16.39\) MeV relative to the \(d+Ω^-\) threshold. The spatial structure is examined through interparticle root-mean-square distances, pair and spectator radial distributions, and the correlation between the two Jacobi coordinates. Relative to a frozen-deuteron folded reference, the full three-body solution exhibits a substantially more compact spectator distribution and a contracted \(pn\) pair. The dependence on the Euclidean-time choice of the HAL QCD potential is also assessed. The results characterize the three-body rearrangement induced by the attractive \(NΩ\) interaction within the adopted pairwise model.

♻ ☆ Mass and decay angles in the $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
Sanghoon Kim, Gihwan Nam, Jongheon Baek
We compare three definitions of $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing within a constituent-quark model: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the two operator-based definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The operator-based angles are closer to the lattice determinations $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$, but remain larger. We then couple conventional $qsQ$ states to virtual $qsQg$ configurations, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. An orbital-$S$-wave chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability stays below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. Eliminating the hybrid sector gives a rank-one mass correction precisely when all weighted transitions select the same retained-state combination. The mode-resolved calculation separates the flavor-breaking response that changes the mixing angle from the response that generates a second transition direction. The accompanying effective-current relation connects this mass analysis to radiative and semileptonic amplitudes through their current matrix elements.

♻ ☆ Hadron properties at finite temperature
Juan M. Torres-Rincon, Glòria Montaña
This review provides an overview of thermal effects on hadron properties, focusing on the theoretical frameworks used to describe in-medium modifications of masses, decay widths, and spectral functions. We examine the application of finite-temperature quantum field theory---specifically the imaginary-time formalism (ITF)---to analyze both light- and heavy-hadron sectors. For light hadrons, we discuss the role of chiral symmetry restoration and the different definitions of thermal masses in effective field theories, like chiral perturbation theory. In the heavy-flavor sector, we review recent progress in describing open-heavy mesons and quarkonia using self-consistent unitarized approaches and nonrelativistic effective field theories. All these results are complemented by analyses of recent lattice-QCD calculations using the Euclidean formulation of QCD at finite temperature, relevant to extracting screening masses and reconstructing spectral functions. Finally, we discuss the phenomenological impact of the thermal modifications on experimental observables in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, including numerical simulations, dilepton spectra, transport coefficients, and hadron femtoscopy. By combining phenomenological considerations with robust theoretical tools, this review provides a coherent picture of how thermal effects emerge in the hadronic phase and how they can be systematically studied within controlled frameworks. Ultimately, the discussion serves as a bridge between experimental observations in relativistic heavy-ion collisions and fundamental developments in finite-temperature QCD and effective field theories for hadronic systems.

♻ ☆ Coupled charm and charmonium transport in a strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma
Kaiyu Fu, Biaogang Wu, Ralf Rapp
The quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is a strongly coupled medium in which both open and hidden charm particles experience substantial nonperturbative interactions. This poses a major challenge for a quantitative description of charmonium transport in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, as it requires a mutually consistent treatment of pertinent transport coefficients. In this work, we present a coupled charm-charmonium transport framework for a strongly coupled QGP based on thermodynamic $T$-matrix interactions with recent constraints from Wilson-line correlators (WLCs) computed in lattice QCD. For the first time, the same underlying heavy-light interactions and in-medium spectral functions are used to self-consistently evaluate charm-quark diffusion and charmonium kinetics. In particular, the charmonium equilibrium limit, a critical transport parameter for regeneration, is evaluated in the presence of broad spectral functions. Charm-quark diffusion is simulated via Langevin dynamics and coupled to a Boltzmann equation for charmonium dissociation and regeneration. The equilibrium limit of the statistical model is recovered once charm quarks thermalize, and its extension to describe off-equilibrium is constructed. Preliminary applications to charmonium observables in Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC capture the measured centrality and momentum dependence fairly well.

♻ ☆ Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
Wan Wu
We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

♻ ☆ Microscopic Spin-Parity Distributions of Fission Fragments
Guillaume Scamps, Petar Marević, Antonio Bjelčić, Nicolas Schunck
Recent microscopic studies have investigated various features of the spin distributions of fission fragments, but their parity distributions remain largely unexplored. In this Letter, we provide a complete characterization of the spin--parity content of fission fragments within a time-dependent Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov framework, performing for the first time simultaneous projections on angular momentum, particle number, and parity. Calculations are carried out for the thermal neutron-induced fission of $^{239}$Pu using both the Gogny and Skyrme energy density functionals. We find that dynamical pair breaking during fission populates a significant fraction of unnatural-parity states and generates components with non-zero spin projections $K$. The parity content is found to depend on the number parity of the fragments, with odd-mass nuclei exhibiting pronounced parity staggering and odd-odd nuclei favoring negative parity. These results show that the parity distribution of fragments can depart significantly from the equiprobable partition commonly assumed in statistical de-excitation models, with potential implications for the modeling of fragment decay.
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures
♻ ☆ Systematic Parameter Optimization of Quantum Molecular Dynamics Models Using Multi-Ion Fragmentation Data: Implications for Hadron Therapy
Akihiro Haga, Yoshi-hide Sato, Daiyu Fujiwara, Dousatsu Sakata, Yuki Tominaga, David Bolst, Edward C. Simpson, Susanna Guatelli
Quantum molecular dynamics (QMD) models are widely used to simulate nuclear fragmentation in hadron therapy, but their predictive accuracy depends strongly on parameters that are often selected empirically. We developed an optimized QMD framework by systematically calibrating three parameters for a relativistic mean-field model with the NS2 parameter set and Skyrme models with the SLy4 and SkM* parameter sets: the wave-packet width L, maximum evolution time Tm, and impact-parameter envelope factor benv. The wave-packet width was determined from experimental charge radii, whereas Tm and benv were parameterized as functions of incident kinetic energy and reaction-system mass and optimized using proton- and heavy-ion-induced fragmentation data over 30-400 MeV/u. Performance was compared with the original LiQMD, Binary Cascade, and Liege Intranuclear Cascade models. The optimized Tm depended strongly on incident energy but only weakly on system mass, indicating that the transition from the dynamical QMD stage to statistical de-excitation is governed mainly by collision energy. In contrast, benv showed model-dependent behavior: NS2 favored larger peripheral-collision contributions for lighter systems at low energies, whereas the Skyrme models showed relatively weak energy and mass dependence. The optimized parameterizations improved agreement with experimental fragment production cross sections, angular distributions, and energy distributions. The optimized Skyrme models achieved the best overall performance and outperformed the cascade models for most datasets. This framework provides a physically consistent description of nuclear fragmentation across multiple observables and may improve calculations of secondary-particle transport, dose deposition, and linear energy transfer in hadron therapy.

♻ ☆ From Lead to Helium: Potential for a Measurement of Jet Quenching in the Smallest Collision Systems
Coleridge Faraday, Ben Bert, Jack Brand, Werner Vogelsang, W. A. Horowitz
We present perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) predictions for the modification to the yield of high-momentum particles in very light ion collisions - ${}^{10}\mathrm{B} + {}^{10}\mathrm{B}$, ${}^{6}\mathrm{Li} + {}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$, ${}^{4}\mathrm{He} + {}^{4}\mathrm{He}$, and ${}^{3}\mathrm{He} + {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ - both with and without medium-induced energy loss. We show that there is non-trivial suppression expected from our partonic energy loss model in symmetric systems from ${}^{208}\mathrm{Pb} + {}^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ to ${}^{3}\mathrm{He} + {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ and in asymmetric systems $A + B$, and that the energy loss scales approximately with $(\sqrt{A B})^{1 / 3}$. Further, we find that deep inelastic scattering measurements in ${}^{3}\mathrm{He}$ and ${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$ tightly constrain the nPDF baseline, making these isotopes a particularly clean environment for searching for final-state partonic energy loss induced by the formation of a quark-gluon plasma in these very small systems.

♻ ☆ Charged pion production in the annihilation reactions $e^+ + e^- \to p + \bar{n} +π^-$ and $e^+ + e^- \to n + \bar{p} +π^+.$ Contribution of the nonresonant mechanism
M. I. Konchatnij, N. P. Merenkov
The nonresonant mechanism in the reactions $e^+\,e^-\to π^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ and $e^+\,e^-\to π^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ is investigated in frame of the one-photon exchange approximation. The description of the hadronic phase space and the invariant amplitude formalism, earlier developed for the neutral pion channel, are applied here. Some modification is required to fulfill the conservation of the hadron electromagnetic current and to account for an additional contribution due to diagram with the pion pole. The double and single distributions over the invariant variables as well the total cross section, are obtained. The results are plotted for $s=$5,\,10,\,16\, GeV$^2$. The calculations are performed for the $π^-\,p\,\bar{n}$ channel and the rules to proceed to the $π^+\,n\,\bar{p}$ channel are formulated for every distribution.

♻ ☆ Anisotropic hybrid stars: Interplay of superconductivity and magnetic field leading to gravitational waves
Zenia Zuraiq, Banibrata Mukhopadhyay
Neutron stars, at their cores, are highly dense and, thus, are expected to have a number of exotic processes. This includes a possible phase transition to deconfined quark matter at the core, leading to a hybrid star. The quark matter is expected to additionally be color superconducting. The physics of superconductivity plays an important role in understanding the high density matter in the interiors of neutron/hybrid stars. At their high densities, additionally, both proton superconductivity and neutron superfluidity are expected. We study the effect of superconducting (quark/proton) matter, along with the internal magnetic field, leading to pressure anisotropy within hybrid stars. We aim to probe the effect of superconductivity, especially from color superconducting quarks, on hybrid star structure. We propose new phenomenological model anisotropy profiles within a one-dimensional framework. We model quark matter using the vector interaction enhanced Bag model, and hadron matter with the DD2 equation of state. A Maxwell construction joins both phases. We further investigate the possible observational signatures of these hybrid stars. These include mass enhancement and the possibility of continuous gravitational waves arising from the anisotropy induced deformation, giving us a way to further constrain our model and its physical parameters.

♻ ☆ Probing the nonstrange quark star equation of state with compact stars and gravitational waves
Shu-Peng Wang, Zhen-Yan Lu, Zhi-Jun Ma, Rong-Yao Yang, Jian-Feng Xu, Xiangyun Fu
A recent study shows that incorporating a new term into the thermodynamic potential density, as required by the thermodynamic consistency criterion, can effectively resolve the thermodynamic inconsistency problems of the conventional perturbative QCD model. This additional term plays a crucial role in resolving inconsistencies at relatively low densities and becomes negligible at extremely high densities. Within this revised perturbative QCD model, we find that if we require only that the energy per baryon of up-down ($ud$) quark matter exceeds 930 MeV so as not to contradict the standard nuclear physics, the maximum mass of an $ud$ quark star allowed by the revised perturbative QCD model can reach up to 2.17 $M_{\odot}$. From this perspective, the observed 2.14 $M_{\odot}$ pulsar PSR J0740+6620 may be an $ud$ quark star. However, if we further impose the constraint that the tidal deformability of a 1.4 $M_{\odot}$ $ud$ quark star must be consistent with the GW170817 event, the maximum mass allowed by the revised perturbative QCD model would decrease to no more than 2.08 $M_{\odot}$. Consequently, our results suggest that the compact object with a mass of 2.50-2.67 $M_{\odot}$, as observed in the GW190814 event, cannot be an $ud$ quark star, according to the revised perturbative QCD model.

☆ Measurements of inclusive $J/ψ$ production in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
The STAR Collaboration

☆ UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation

A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings. It is therefore particularly relevant for loop correlators with soft external modes. In both cases, the additional corrections induced by the inhomogeneous cutoff cancel the ultraviolet boundary terms arising in the ordinary diagrams. These calculations establish, within cutoff regularization, the late-time constancy of both power spectra and clarify its physical origin. We then investigate the squeezed one-loop scalar bispectrum and show that the additional cutoff contributions are essential for satisfying the consistency relation at finite cutoff. Finally, we discuss the role of the inhomogeneous cutoff in the late-time constancy of the one-loop bispectrum.

Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.

In multi-field PD, the dressed tadpole is not a gradient, so the reconstructed potential depends on the integration path. In benchmark tests, changing the path shifts the transition temperatures by at most about 7% and the peak amplitude by up to a factor of about three. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $Δm^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $Δm^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $ν_μ$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$, and the $ν_μ$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $θ_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy range, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|Δm^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $δ_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$ and $θ_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.

♻ ☆ The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
Ondrej Chvala
The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969, and Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD. Regge exchange organizes the fragmentation region in triple-Regge form and supplies the diffractive mass law of the excited systems. Finite-energy sum rules and the two-component duality of Harari and Freund equate averaged towers of resonances with that exchange. Duality therefore motivates describing the excited systems in hadronic degrees of freedom. The cascade description has five predecessors, namely the fireballs of Niu, the novas of Jacob and Slansky, the clusters of Hwa, Good-Walker diffraction, and the two-stage dissociation of Hama. A companion paper (arXiv:2611.11570) assembles these pieces into HEART (Hadronic Excitations And Resonance Transitions), an event-level cascade of two-body hadronic transitions, and fits it to the NA49 data. The review closes with the fragmentation-region measurements that would separate a resonance cascade from a string, namely the isospin of forward baryons, local strangeness balance, and forward resonance signals.

In this framework, the scalar potential admits CP-related degenerate vacua, leading to the formation of CP domain walls. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

The resulting signal rate depends on both the production cross sections and the physical invisible branching fractions. The inclusive rates of $3.33$ and $1.43$~fb at loop-induced leading order provide quantitative signal targets before the visible Higgs decay and analysis cuts. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $κ$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $ω=mΩ_{\rm H}-ijκ$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $Ω_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. These local statements leave the QNM spectrum unchanged but matter for merger ringdowns, because a source falling through the horizon drives the exterior at the horizon frequencies. Each QNM then has a driven and a free part, and the free part takes over only once the driving decays faster than the mode. The fundamental mode separates from the driving early. The overtones stay driven until the source is hidden behind the potential barrier, so overtone amplitudes fitted near the signal peak are in general not those of free oscillations. In GW250114, a ringdown model of the fundamental mode plus the first horizon mode, $ω=2Ω_{\rm H}-iκ$, is preferred over the fundamental mode plus its first overtone, with Bayes factors between 2 and 30, for start times from $2M_f$ before to $8M_f$ after coalescence. The horizon-mode fit returns a remnant that is heavier and spins faster than the inspiral predicts, as expected from nonlinear backreaction: the horizon that emits the mode has not yet settled to its final mass and spin. Zero-noise injections of numerical-relativity-calibrated waveforms reproduce both the preference and the shift, which are therefore features of general relativity.

We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.

☆ Critical droplets and metastability in long-range chains
Laura Batini, Valerio Pagni, Nicolò Defenu
Metastable decay in first-order phase transitions proceeds through the nucleation of critical droplets. In the one-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising chain, the cost of the two walls bounding a droplet is independent of its size. For interactions decaying as $1/r^{1+σ}$, this surface cost instead depends on the droplet size and competes with the bulk free-energy gain. The critical radius scales as $R_c\propto h^{-1/σ}$ at small $h$, where $h>0$ is the bias field. The value $σ=1$ separates two regimes: for $σ<1$, the activation barrier diverges as $h\to0^+$; at $σ=1$, it grows logarithmically; and for $σ>1$, it remains finite, as in the nearest-neighbor chain. A nonlocal $φ^4$ field theory yields critical droplets with algebraic tails and confirms the predicted radius and barrier scalings, while stochastic long-range dynamics independently reproduces the critical-radius scaling.

☆ Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
Kazuya Yonekura
Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.

☆ Two Faces of Spacetime Density Matrices: Entanglement and Complexity
Wu-zhong Guo
We establish a direct connection between entanglement and complexity through spacetime density matrices. For stationary pure states and complementary regions at different times, spacetime replica moments encode the return amplitude of a replica-defect quench. This representation defines an associated state spread complexity, which we call Krylov-Rényi complexity. It can equivalently be obtained by using a replica-defect excitation of the replicated background state as the seed and evolving it under the original replicated Hamiltonian. We further construct Krylov-von Neumann complexity as a probe limit from first-order replica data. Timelike entanglement and complexity provide complementary information at a fixed time, while the full time dependence of the timelike entropy determines the Krylov dynamics and hence the complexity. The replica construction fixes the seed and its evolution through the background state, subsystem geometry, and regulator, without an independently chosen probe operator. Like entanglement entropy, the resulting complexity is defined nonperturbatively and probes universal properties and dynamical information about the underlying theory.

☆ A full-color four-point form factor

We determine the symbol and complete functions of the full-color two-loop four-point maximally helicity violating stress-tensor form factor in $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, including $N^1$ double traces and $N^0$ single traces. Numerical unitarity and a master-integral bootstrap fix the result. A direct form-factor bootstrap reproduces the symbol. Permuting external legs in the planar 88-letter alphabet yields all 79 letters, while the $N^0$ terms contain four new nonclassical contributions. We also obtain the complete $N^0$ two-loop triple-collinear hard splitting functions.

☆ From Integrability to Chaos in Tensionless AdS3 String Theory

We study quantum-gravitational corrections to the planar integrable structure of the symmetric product orbifold $\text{Sym}^N(\mathbb{T}^4)$ that is dual to tensionless string theory on AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times \mathbb{T}^4$. We consider the deformation that switches on R-R flux in the bulk, and analyze the associated level spacing statistics. The leading non-planar corrections lift the planar degeneracies and produce signs of random-matrix behavior. Our results provide a controlled example of string interactions driving the onset of quantum chaos.

☆ Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
Sahil Chetan Patnekar, Sristi Sanjivanee Goswami, Sanjay Pant, Shagun Kaushal
We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.

☆ Upper Bounds on the Radion Mass in a Warped Extra Dimension
Leandro Da Rold, Eugenio Megias, Mariano Quiros, Lindber Salas
We study absolute upper bounds on the mass ratio $R_{11}=m_{r_1}/m_{h_1}$ between the radion ($r_1$) and graviton ($h_1$) lightest modes in five dimensional warped models. We consider warped models with an admissible singular behavior in the infrared: i.e.~models with power-like ($\sim \barφ^{2n}$) and with exponential ($\sim e^{2ν\barφ}$) bulk potentials, where $\barφ$ is the stabilizing bulk field. We find a correlation between $R_{11}$ and the singular behavior of the Ricci scalar, which allows to establish an absolute upper bound on the former. For the power-like models, the maximum value of $R_{11}$ increases with $n$. In the limit $n\to\infty$, the power-like model reproduces the exponential model and reaches the same upper bound as the latter. For the exponential model, we derive analytically the bound $R_{11}<1$, with the largest value approached for the case $ν\to 1^+$ (where $ν=1$ corresponds to the linear dilaton model) and consistent with unitarity sum rules. For exponential models we also obtain the absolute upper bound on the second radion mode ratio $R_{21}=m_{r_2}/m_{h_1}\lesssim 1.374$. This value is reached for $ν=2$ when the IR brane approaches the singularity. For this configuration, we verify that the scalar contribution satisfies the unitarity sum rule when the complete radion Kaluza-Klein tower is included.

☆ Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
Akira Otsuki, Yuta Yamamoto, Kokin Cho, Rikuto Fushio, Masahito Yamazaki
Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $χ$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $χ$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.

♻ ☆ Preheating and oscillon formation in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
Areef Waeming, Josu C. Aurrekoetxea, Katy Clough, Pau Figueras, Áron D. Kovács
Non-perturbative processes in the early universe may create overdense structures in scalar fields like the inflaton, called oscillons. In this work, we explore whether the leading order higher derivative contributions to the scalar-tensor theory change the formation and growth of these structures, and investigate the limits in which the effective field theory (EFT) description breaks down. We find that whilst the properties of the oscillons are not significantly modified, and black holes do not generically form, for large couplings the period of formation can result in the evolution leaving the regime of validity of the EFT, at which point predictivity is lost and the next order terms in the EFT should become relevant. If the oscillons survive their formation, they tend to be stable and the EFT corrections remain bounded. The EFT breakdown is triggered by large curvature terms in the metric in the densest regions of the oscillon, meaning that approximations of such modified theories that neglect the local backreaction and non-linear dynamics of the fields may miss important effects.
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures. Matches the version published in PRD
♻ ☆ Holographic warped CFTs on AdS$_3$, parity violation and unitarity
Kristiansen Lara, Ricardo Troncoso
We consider recently introduced boundary conditions for General Relativity on AdS$_3$, whose canonical generators span the warped conformal algebra, in the case of the Einstein-Hilbert action supplemented by parity-odd terms that do not modify the field equations in vacuum. The canonical generators are shown to acquire nonlinear contributions, and their algebra remains being the semidirect sum of Virasoro and $u(1)$ Kac-Moody, but with shifted central extensions. Thus, for suitable values of the parity-odd coupling, the Kac-Moody level can be nonnegative ($k_\text{KM}\geq 0$), admitting unitary representations. Nevertheless, requiring the black hole entropy to be nonnegative, implies $k_\text{KM}\leq 0$, in agreement with the established understanding of holographic warped CFTs. Compatibility of both requirements (entropy and unitarity) then singles out the case $k_\text{KM}=0$. However, the field equations degenerate in this case, which can be amended by imposing vanishing torsion as a constraint. The theory then precisely becomes Topologically Massive Gravity (TMG) at the chiral point, suggesting the extension of our boundary conditions to accommodate nontrivial logarithmic branches.

♻ ☆ Gravitational Duals from Equations of State II: Large Hierarchies and False Vacua
Raul Jimenez, David Mateos, Pavlos Protopapas, Pau Solé-Vilaró, Pedro Tarancón-Álvarez, Pablo Tejerina-Pérez
We investigate the reconstruction of holographic duals for strongly coupled quantum field theories in regimes characterized by large hierarchies and the presence of false vacua. Within the gauge/gravity duality, these features translate into non-trivial thermodynamic behaviour and exotic renormalization group flows, including skipping flows between non-adjacent fixed points. Building on previous work based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), we extend the holographic inverse problem of reconstructing the bulk scalar potential from boundary thermodynamic data into this new regime. This setting presents a variety of conceptual and numerical challenges, such as near-degenerate states, large hierarchies of energy scales, and regions of the potential that are not directly probed by the input data. We develop a set of methodological advances that overcome these obstacles, thereby improving the established PINNs-based methodology and extending it to new physical regimes of interest that were previously out of reach. Applying the developed framework, we demonstrate accurate reconstruction of scalar potentials deep into the false vacuum regime, achieving robust agreement with the physical features of the underlying thermodynamics despite significant numerical stiffness. Our results extend the bridge between holography and machine learning, and suggest that data-driven approaches can provide new insights into the structure of strongly coupled systems.

♻ ☆ Probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism with low-frequency gravitational waves
Debasish Borah, Sounak Dutta, Partha Kumar Paul, Indrajit Saha, Narendra Sahu
We study the possibility of probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism for the origin of light neutrino masses via the detection of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) in the low-frequency regime currently being probed by pulsar timing arrays. As the lepton number-violating term in inverse seesaw typically remains in the sub-MeV ballpark, its dynamical origin naturally brings the possibility of a low-scale first-order phase transition, which can be probed at low-frequency GW experiments. We also find interesting complementarity with heavy neutral lepton searches, as GW experiments remain sensitive to parameter space with small active-sterile mixing, which is out of reach for most particle physics experiments.

♻ ☆ Kerr-Newman and genuine Kerr black holes in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field
Hryhorii Ovcharenko, Jiri Podolsky
We present a spacetime that describes a rotating and charged black hole immersed in an external magnetic (or electric) field which is oriented along the rotational axis. This solution is characterized by four physical parameters, namely the black hole mass $m$, its charge $e$, Kerr-like rotation $a$, and the value of the external field $B$. Such exact solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations has a surprisingly simple form. Moreover, for $B=0$ it reduces to standard Kerr-Newman metric, while for $m=0$ and $e=0$ we recover the Bertotti-Robinson universe with a uniform (electro-)magnetic field. We also show that the Kerr-BR solution presented in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 181401 (2025)] has a special charge, and we identify a genuine uncharged Kerr black hole immersed in the magnetic field. In the weak-field limit, it gives the Wald solution. We analyze the main physical properties of the new family, namely singularities, horizons, regularity of axes, charges, entropy, and temperature.

♻ ☆ Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti
In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).
comment: Improved Version, 19 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ A major origin of quantumness
Gerd Niestegge
A system property is considered to be elementary, when any further refined specification is impossible. Any two elementary properties of a classical system mutually exclude each other. However, this does not hold anymore for a quantum system, where mutual exclusivity becomes a special relation. This orthogonality relation becomes our first axiom. It is sufficient to define states in an abstract setting and we then introduce two simple, but far-reaching further basic axioms for the states, which mimic the quantum mechanical correspondence between the pure states and the rank-one projections. All examples that we can identify origin from operator algebras or certain Jordan algebras and require the Gleason theorem. The identification of further cases is an unresolved challenge. If some exist, they might result in promising new mathematical models for an extended quantum theory. The non-existence would mean that our extremely basic postulates bring us unexpectedly close to common quantum theory. In any case, the distinction between inequality and mutual exclusivity of elementary system properties appears to be a major origin of quantumness. Our basic approach does not encompass the non-atomic von Neumann algebras of type II and III, which play a crucial role in quantum field theory, and we present a modification of the axioms to include them.
comment: New title, new content; 14 pages; comments and contributions very welcome
♻ ☆ Multiscale Renormalization of Weighted Networks
Mattia Marzi, Frank P. Pijpers, Diego Garlaschelli
Recent progress in network renormalization has identified various ways to transform network representations consistently across resolution levels. In particular, the renormalization flow describing how random graph models transform under node aggregation has identified a fixed point corresponding to an aggregation-invariant model that preserves the form of the connection probability across arbitrary scales. While this probabilistic multiscale approach has successfully been used to model real-world networks, construct latent-space node embeddings, and reconstruct finer-grained versions of aggregate network data in a principled resolution-invariant way, it has so far been restricted to binary graphs. Here we reformulate multiscale network renormalization for weighted random graphs. Via a generating-function approach, we identify a weighted multiscale model whose full probability law, encoding both link creation and weight assignment, has an invariant compound-Poisson form under arbitrary node aggregation. The renormalization rules that transform parameters across aggregation levels allow the ensemble to be calibrated at one level and applied at another, enabling consistent modeling and reconstruction of weighted networks across arbitrary scales.

The structure of divergences in several nonpolynomial scalar quantum field theories are investigated. Various $n$-point Green functions for nonpolynomial theories are calculated and their renormalization is analyzed, with special regard for the nonpolynomial $\left|φ\right|^{3}$ theory in $4$ spacetime dimensions.

♻ ☆ Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string integrals from the intersection matrix

We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.

♻ ☆ Neural-Spectral Discovery of Rotating Black Holes Beyond General Relativity
Felipe Agurto-Sepúlveda, Marcelo Oyarzo, Anxo Biasi, Devansh Agarwal, Ethan Tregidga, James F. Steiner, Jose D. Edelstein, Gaston Giribet, Cecilia Garraffo
Finding rotating black hole solutions in higher-curvature theories of gravity is a problem of fundamental importance. Virtually every approach to reconcile gravity with quantum mechanics predicts corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yet no systematic solution-generating method exists for the stationary sector. We close this gap with Akribeia, a novel hybrid framework that pairs physics-informed neural networks with a pseudo-spectral refinement step, yielding certified neural-field rotating black hole solutions ---continuous, globally defined functions, parametric in the coupling constants--- whose residuals against the field equations are verified to extreme precision. We apply the method to theories quadratic and cubic in the curvature and construct, for the first time, families of rotating black holes featuring multiple non-vanishing angular momenta, parametric in the new coupling constants. After validating against previously known five-dimensional spacetimes, we present new solutions in scenarios leading to a highly non-linear/non-perturbative coupled system of ordinary differential equations. Our method can be systematically adapted to other setups involving partial differential equations as well.

We propose quantum differential equations (QDEs) for periods of nonabelian mirror theories and develop an algorithm for constructing them directly from the mirrors. We verify the proposal by recovering known quantum differential equations of Grassmannians and Picard-Fuchs equations of Calabi-Yau complete intersections in Grassmannians. Our algorithm applies to a broad class of nonabelian GLSMs and yields new examples of quantum differential equations for several Fano varieties. The associated cohomology-valued generating functions can be extracted directly from these equations. Using them, we compute instanton numbers of both complete-intersection and non-complete-intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds, including the Pfaffian and Gulliksen--Negård Calabi-Yau threefolds. The resulting instanton numbers agree with all previously known computations, while the generating functions obtained for the non-complete-intersection examples are new.

♻ ☆ Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
Wan Wu
We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.

♻ ☆ False vacuum decay in long-range interacting quantum systems
Valerio Pagni, Laura Batini, Nicolò Defenu
We formulate false-vacuum decay in a mixed-field Ising chain with $r^{-(1+σ)}$ interactions as a spatially nonlocal Euclidean $φ^4$ theory featuring a fractional spatial kinetic term $\sim |q|^σ$. The nonlocal bounce is anisotropic in space-time and develops algebraic spatial tails. Combining thin-wall arguments with numerical solutions of the full nonlocal saddle, we find two nucleation regimes separated by $σ= 1$. For $0<σ<1$, the lifetime exponent scales with the energy bias $h$ of the metastable state as $B\sim h^{-1/σ}$; for $1<σ<2$, the leading Coleman scaling $B\sim h^{-1}$ is recovered, while long-range effects are retained in the subleading correction $\sim h^{σ-2}$. The same exponents are recovered directly within a two-kink description of the Ising chain on the lattice. Our results show that tunable long-range interactions fundamentally reshape bubble nucleation and alter false-vacuum decay in quantum simulators.
♻ ☆ Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
Ben Gripaios
We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.
comment: 7pp. v2: added discussion of lines in smooth nondegenerate fibres
♻ ☆ Stochastic Survival near Swampland Boundaries
Omer Guleryuz
Swampland and compactification data tell us where a chosen EFT description can lose parametric control; stochastic cosmology asks which histories survive near that edge. We turn this question into a survival problem for fluctuating moduli over cosmological time scales. Given a valid stochastic generator, hard loss surfaces, soft degradation profiles, and finite horizons define a survival probability, whose negative logarithm is the survival action. The Doob transform then converts this logarithmic survival cost into the drift of the ensemble conditioned to remain on the controlled side. Near a regular hard boundary with nonzero normal diffusion, the inward normal component of the conditioned response is universal: it is fixed at leading order by the proper distance to the wall and the normal diffusion coefficient. The same finite-horizon construction also determines loss probabilities, first-exit statistics, survival hazards, and the control margin required to retain a prescribed fraction of histories. In this way, tower/species cutoffs, weak-coupling limits, string and Kaluza-Klein thresholds, and carefully qualified potential-based diagnostics acquire stochastic boundary layers without becoming microscopic forces. The inverse map tests when a conditioned drift is compatible with a scalar operational loss surface and reconstructs its boundary-normal Doob class. The construction therefore gives a stochastic survival interface between quantum-gravity control data and the cosmological histories that remain inside the prescribed EFT domain.

♻ ☆ Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities

We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

♻ ☆ A measure on the space of CFTs and pure 3D gravity
Alexandre Belin, Alexander Maloney, Florian Seefeld
We define a normalizable measure on subspaces of two-dimensional conformal field theories, which we interpret as a maximum ignorance ensemble. These subspaces are specified by a range of allowed central charges and a minimum gap on the scaling dimension of operators. We test whether pure quantum gravity in AdS3 is dual to the average over this ensemble. We find a negative answer, which implies that CFTs with a primary gap of order the central charge are highly atypical in our ensemble. We provide evidence that more generally, holographic CFTs are atypical in the space of all CFTs by finding similar results for permutation orbifolds: subgroups of SN with a good large N limit are very sparse in the space of all subgroups. Along the way, we derive several new results on the space of CFTs. Notably we derive an upper bound on the spacing in central charge between CFTs, which is doubly exponentially small in the large central charge limit.

♻ ☆ Monopoles, Strings, Walls and Gravitational waves
Rinku Maji, Qaisar Shafi
The gauge symmetry breaking $SU(2) \to U(1) \to Z_2 \to 1$ successively produces monopoles, strings and domain walls bounded by strings (WBS), with the elementary monopole carrying a $U(1)$ magnetic flux twice as large as the elementary string. The elementary strings and subsequently WBS emit gravitational waves, and during their decay, the WBS yield a network of composite strings that carry the same $U(1)$ flux as the monopoles. Depending on the cosmological evolution, we provide the gravitational wave spectra generated by the elementary strings and WBS, in combination with the composite strings which are either effectively stable, quasistable, or metastable. These three scenarios are also realized in the symmetry breaking chain $SU(3) \to SO(3) \to Z_2 \to 1$. Both $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ have appeared in the literature as flavor gauge symmetries.

♻ ☆ Hidden Conformal Boundary Data in Finite-Temperature Stabilizer Entropy
Reyhaneh Khasseh, M. A. Rajabpour
We study the finite-temperature stabilizer Rényi entropy of the open critical transverse-field Ising chain. At Rényi index one half, this observable probes the distribution of thermal Pauli-string expectation values and can be written as a sum over absolute values of all square minors of a finite-temperature correlation matrix. We show that this exponentially large sum is exactly reducible to a single Pfaffian. The Pfaffian representation reveals a block Toeplitz--Hankel structure and allows us to extract the large-size scaling in several thermal regimes. In the crossover window where the inverse temperature is proportional to the system size, the stabilizer numerator factorizes into a saturated extensive contribution and a universal finite-size scaling function. We find that this scaling function is a level-eight eta quotient, rather than the ordinary free-boundary Majorana thermal factor. We identify it with the normalized midpoint disorder-field one-point function of the free-boundary Ising CFT. The deviation is exponentially hidden at low temperature but becomes manifest in the small-\(τ\) modular limit, where it gives a Cardy-like asymptotic for the Pauli-string expectation-weight spectrum. These results show that finite-temperature stabilizer entropy probes a universal Ising disorder-field amplitude that is invisible to ordinary thermodynamic probes.

♻ ☆ Quantum gravitodiamagnetic interaction
Di Hao, Jiawei Hu, Hongwei Yu
In the framework of linearized quantum gravity, we investigate the quantum gravitational interaction induced by the gravitodiamagnetic coupling of two massive objects to vacuum fluctuations of the gravitational field. Starting from the Lagrangian of a particle in a gravitational field and employing the formalism of Weyl gravitoelectromagnetism, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian associated with gravitodiamagnetic coupling. Unlike the linear couplings that arise in gravitoelectric and gravitomagnetic interactions, the gravitodiamagnetic coupling depends quadratically on the gravitomagnetic field. Based on this Hamiltonian, we show that, for a spherically symmetric gravitational hydrogen-like system in its ground state, the induced quadrupole moment has the opposite sign to the applied gravitomagnetic field, which is the defining signature of gravitodiamagnetism. Using leading-order perturbation theory, we derive an explicit expression for the gravitodiamagnetic interaction potential, valid for $r\gg a$, where $r$ is the separation and $a$ the characteristic size of the objects. Unlike previously studied quantum gravitational interactions, which exhibit distinct power laws in the near and far regions defined relative to the characteristic transition wavelength of the gravitational hydrogen-like systems, the gravitodiamagnetic interaction is attractive and scales as $r^{-11}$ throughout its regime of validity.
