♻ ☆ On co-dimension 2 defect anomalies in N=4 SYM and (2,0) theory via brane probes in AdS/CFT
Hongliang Jiang, Arkady A. Tseytlin
We consider a half-BPS solution for a D3 brane probe in AdS$_5 \times S^5$ that has world-volume geometry of AdS$_3 \times S^1$. It intersects the boundary over a surface that represents a dimension 2 defect in the boundary ${\cal N}=4$ SYM theory. The effective action of the probe brane is proportional to the logarithmically divergent volume of AdS$_3$ and may thus be interpreted as computing conformal anomaly of supersymmetric $S^2$ defect. The classical action scales as $N$. We compute the 1-loop correction to it due to quantum fluctuations of the D3 brane world-volume fields and compare the result to an earlier suggested expression for the defect anomaly. With the boundary condition for the zero mode of the world-volume vector required by supersymmetry the sum over the modes gives the 1-loop coefficient $-3$ instead of the expected $-6$. We suggest that the remaining part is due to the classical response of the background to the probe. We also perform a similar analysis of a half-BPS supersymmetric M5 brane probe solution in AdS$_7 \times S^4$ with the world-volume geometry of AdS$_5 \times S^1$ that represents a dimension 4 defect in the boundary (2,0) 6d theory. Here the classical M5 brane action computes the leading order $N^2$ term in $a$-anomaly of the supersymmetric $S^4$ defect. The fluctuations form a tower of chiral multiplets and a flavour current multiplet of the 4d ${\cal N}=2$ superconformal symmetry. We perform a detailed computation of the 1-loop correction to the M5 brane effective action and discuss prescription dependence of the prediction for the contribution to the $S^4$ defect $a$-anomaly coefficient.

♻ ☆ Interplay between the chiral and deconfinement transitions from a Curci-Ferrari-based Polyakov loop potential
V. Tomas Mari Surkau, Urko Reinosa
We couple the two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model to a gluonic background corresponding to the gauge-field expectation value in the center-symmetric Landau gauge. Low-energy features in this gauge are captured by a center-symmetric extension of the Curci-Ferrari model and provide a good grasp on key aspects of the confinement/deconfinement transition. Within this framework, we can investigate the interplay between the chiral and deconfinement transitions. Compared to other approaches based on multi-parameter Ansätze of the Polyakov loop potential fixed from comparison to finite-temperature lattice data, the modeling of the glue sector in the present set-up depends on only one phenomenological parameter that can be fixed by comparison to lattice data in the vacuum. We detail the structure of the phase diagram, with special emphasis on the finite density axis, and compute thermodynamical observables relevant for applications. We also highlight the properties of the recently introduced net quark number response of the medium as a sensible probe of the phases of QCD, in particular as a tool to disambiguate the nature of certain regions of the phase diagram where the use of the Polyakov loops could lead to misinterpretations. Finally, we critically assess the sensitivity of our results to the various parameters, both in the glue sector and in the chiral sector.

♻ ☆ Near-horizon modifications in finite $N$ holography
Rishkrith Bairy, Mrityunjay Nath, Debajyoti Sarkar
If one extends the AdS/CFT extrapolate dictionary to large but finite $N$, we are expected to obtain non-perturbative violations of bulk semi-classicality and micro-causality. Previously this was achieved by implementing a late boundary time cut-off, while smearing the boundary operator via the HKLL kernel. By performing explicit bulk reconstructions in the backgrounds of near-horizon modified AdS$_2$ and BTZ black holes, we recover similar deviations from semi-classicality as above. For these black hole mimickers, the near-horizon modification is controlled by a throat parameter which sets the scale of this deviation. In three bulk dimensions, probe dynamics, for a fixed radial band, also exhibits a dip-ramp-plateau structure in their spectral form factor when averaged over the throat parameter. Such structure has also been found recently in the background with a stretched horizon or a brick wall.

♻ ☆ Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal
We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.

♻ ☆ Towards a recursive construction of string scattering amplitudes

We construct open superstring scattering amplitudes from three-point data using the Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten (BCFW) recursion and four-dimensional spinor helicity variables. We compute the contributions of selected leading and subleading Regge families to the color-ordered four-gluon amplitude by sewing their cubic couplings and summing over intermediate polarizations. The four-dimensional description makes helicity selection rules explicit and reduces the massive polarization sums to SU(2) little group contractions. The resulting residues are expressed in terms of Jacobi and Legendre polynomials, yielding explicit sums over mass levels. We construct a differential operator relating the two polynomial kernels, including their level-dependent normalizations. These results provide a concrete starting point for organizing the infinite intermediate-state sum and investigating whether relations among Regge families can support a recursive reconstruction of the full string amplitude.

♻ ☆ The Goldstone Awakens: Unimodular dark energy in scale-invariant $R^2$ gravity
Mariaveronica De Angelis, Javier Rubio
We construct an $R^2$ cosmology based on scale invariance and unimodular gravity in which the Goldstone boson of dilatations establishes a predictive connection between inflation and dark energy. The conservation of the corresponding Noether current confines the inflationary trajectory to a one-dimensional orbit in field space, freezing the Goldstone direction and rendering the inflationary dynamics effectively single field. After inflation, the system settles on a Minkowski vacuum manifold. The unimodular integration constant, already present in the full theory but negligible during inflation, lifts the flat Goldstone direction, generating an exponential potential for the canonically normalised field. Unlike in phenomenological quintessence models, its slope is not a free DE parameter, but is instead fixed by the field-space geometry inherited from the inflationary attractor. This geometry excludes matter-era tracking and, throughout the inflationary viability region, places the field in the thawing regime compatible with accelerated expansion. For a representative inflationary benchmark, the now pseudo-Goldstone field remains frozen until close to the present epoch, yielding DE equation-of-state parameters $(w_0,w_a)\simeq(-0.992,-0.011)$ in the CPL parametrisation $w(a)=w_0+w_a(1-a)$. More generally, the same parameter controlling the inflationary spectral tilt also fixes the slope of the DE potential, leading to a tight correlation between early- and late-Universe observables: increasing the thawing signal lowers $n_s$, while values of $n_s$ closer to unity drive the model towards $Λ$CDM.

♻ ☆ Four-Point String Monodromy from Six-Point Supersymmetric Consistency
Jianqi Sheng
Can finite-particle consistency determine an infinite string amplitude? For four-dimensional planar tree-level $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills effective theories with a specified scalar parity condition, we derive all-order constraints directly from physical six-point Ward identities and local factorization. An overlapping-channel limit forces a scalar cocycle, while an explicit differential Ward functional eliminates all relevant five- and six-point contact freedom and fixes the four-point kernel by $q''=-6c_{00}q$. Its normalized branches are linear, trigonometric, and hyperbolic, and the target amplitude obeys the associated four-point monodromy. If its entire pole-subtracted axis sequence additionally admits one common nonzero positive moment measure, the trigonometric branch is selected and the complete Veneziano low-energy germ is unique up to scale. The result separates a formal low-energy necessity theorem from its conditional analytic-germ uniqueness corollary; no worldsheet or auxiliary KLT-module membership is assumed for the physical theorem.
♻ ☆ Spacetime-Foam Correlations as the Origin of Cosmological-Constant Dark Energy: Their Effects on Cosmological Evolution and Astrophysical Systems
She-Sheng Xue
Wheeler spacetime foam at the Planck scale is characterized by quantum-gravitational fluctuations that create, oscillate, and annihilate microscopic spacetime structures. We model these structures as a Planck-scale lattice using Euclidean quantum gravity on a simplicial complex. Their long-wavelength collective excitations are described by interacting scalar fields, which we call ``foamons,'' in analogy with phonons in a crystal lattice. Through Coleman--Hawking interactions, foamons couple to quantum or classical field operators at scales much larger than the Planck length. These operators provide physical infrared scales that determine the characteristic correlation lengths of the foamon fields. We use a Wilsonian renormalisation-group framework to study their scaling-invariant behaviour near infrared and ultraviolet fixed points. Integrating out the foamon degrees of freedom generates effective actions for physical field operators, with the foamon correlation lengths setting the corresponding macroscopic scales and effective couplings. We apply this framework to cosmology and astrophysics, where the Ricci-scalar sector gives rise to an effective cosmological term $Λ_R\simξ_R^{-2}$ with equation of state $p_Λ\approx -ρ_Λ$. For a cosmological correlation length $ξ_R\sim H^{-1}$, this yields $ρ_{Λ_R}\sim M_{\rm pl}^2H^2$, providing a possible mechanism for the small observed dark-energy scale. The effective cosmological term $Λ_R$ varies in spacetime and interacts with matter through its dependence on the Ricci scalar. We investigate its effects on cosmic evolution, galactic rotation curves, and the deflection of light grazing the solar surface.

For one-row charges we construct the spherical-DAHA operator $\mathbf{e}_+h_r(Y)\mathbf{e}_+$ and determine its finite shift expansion and discrete Macdonald spectrum. For the first non-minuscule $U(2)$ coefficient, a local two-minuscule convolution model with Higgs branch $T^*\mathbb{P}^1$ has two Jeffrey-Kirwan residues, while subtracting the determinant intersection-cohomology summand supplies the additional $-\mathfrak{t}$ term. The same transverse $A_1$ calculation, dressed by the spectator-root factor, reproduces the first lower $U(3)$ coefficient. The two residues are the cross terms of the square of the first Macdonald-Ruijsenaars operator and the subtraction realizes $h_2=e_1^2-e_2$, so that this calculation is a geometric realization of the algebraic coefficient, while its boundary-localization interpretation remains conjectural. We then let the operators act on the evaluation functionals at the points $q^λ\mathfrak{t}^ρ$ with $ρ=(N-1,\ldots,0)$, which for minuscule $λ$ coincide, up to a common factor and the order of the entries, with the fugacities of the Higgsing computation of Hatsuda and Okazaki. The zero-shift coefficient at $\mathfrak{t}^ρ$ of the product of the two oppositely oriented operators equals the normalized Neumann Wilson two-point function for every one-row charge, and for $U(2)$ and $r=2$ this equality requires the $-\mathfrak{t}$ term.

♻ ☆ Gravitational Waves from Superconducting Cosmic Strings

We study the evolution of superconducting cosmic-string networks in a $U(1)_{\rm local}\times U(1)_{\rm global}$ field-theoretic model using three-dimensional lattice field simulations in an expanding universe. The scalar field charged under $U(1)_{\rm local}$ forms cosmic strings, while the scalar field associated with $U(1)_{\rm global}$ acts as a current carrier and condenses in their vicinity. We investigate the evolution of the string network for several values of the coupling constant between the string-forming and current-carrier fields and estimate the gravitational-wave power spectrum sourced by the resulting superconducting cosmic-string network. We find that the spectral shape depends on the coupling constant: as the interaction strength increases, the spectrum is suppressed on small scales. This feature may be probed by future high-frequency gravitational-wave observations.

♻ ☆ Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
Sriram Akella
A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.

♻ ☆ Echoes and light rings of regular black holes and their singular counterparts

Recent work [Phys. Rev. D 111, 104040] showed that the Bardeen and Hayward solutions arise as fine-tuned regular members of broader families that also contain singular black holes. We study massless scalar and auxiliary Maxwell perturbations of these solutions using time-domain evolution and a sixth-order WKB approximation. For part of the singular branch, the time-domain profiles exhibit late-time echoes and the effective potentials develop a double-barrier structure. We also examine null geodesics of the background metric. The same singular branch can have two exterior maxima of the null effective potential separated by a minimum, whereas the type-I regular black holes have a single exterior maximum. The Bardeen and Hayward families display the same qualitative behavior.

♻ ☆ Relationship between a $Φ^4$ matrix model and harmonic oscillator systems

A Hermitian $Φ^4$ matrix model with a Kontsevich-type kinetic term is studied. It was recently discovered that the partition function of this matrix model satisfies the Schrödinger equation of the $N$-body harmonic oscillator, and that eigenstates of the Virasoro operators can be derived from this partition function. We extend these results and obtain an explicit formula for such eigenstates in terms of the free energy. Furthermore, the Schrödinger equation for the $N$-body harmonic oscillator can also be reformulated in terms of connected correlation functions. The $U(1)^N$-symmetry allows us to derive loop equations.

♻ ☆ Higher-Spin dS/CFT beyond minimal type-A, and the doubled nature of de Sitter space
Julian Lang, Yasha Neiman
We study the holographic duality between free vector models and Higher-Spin Gravity in 4-dimensional de Sitter space. On both the bulk and boundary sides, we introduce new reality conditions, which allow us to include odd spins in the bulk, and to extend the duality from type-A to type-B (i.e. from boundary scalars to spinors). The new reality conditions are closely related to a higher-spin-symmetric Hilbert-space norm for the single-particle (super)multiplet in de Sitter space. We construct two alternative viewpoints on the type-A and type-B theories. In one view, the two co-exist in "parallel universes", specifically in even vs. odd antipodal identifications of de Sitter space. In the other view, type-A and type-B are Legendre-transformed descriptions of the same twistor-space theory in Euclidean AdS (this involves the observation that the higher-spin partition function is Legendre-dual to itself). In this way, higher-spin holography reconciles the two-boundary nature of de Sitter space with the one-boundary nature of Euclidean AdS. The supersymmetric theory that unifies type-A and type-B with bulk fermions fails to be consistent under the appropriate reality conditions.

♻ ☆ Mass Varying Neutrino Oscillation in Teleparallel Gravity
H. Mohseni Sadjadi, H. Yazdani Ahmadabadi
In the Cartan teleparallel formulation of gravity, a scalar field coupled to the torsion tensor can acquire an environment-dependent effective mass. This gives rise to a screening effect: inside dense bodies such as the Sun, the scalar field is suppressed, causing the neutrino mass to vary with local density. We investigate the impact of this torsion-induced screening on solar neutrino oscillations. The mechanism modifies the standard MSW resonance condition distinctly, leading to detectable shifts in the flavor conversion probability. Using data from solar neutrino experiments (Super-Kamiokande, Borexino, SNO), we place constraints on the torsion scalar coupling parameters. Our work provides a concrete test of teleparallel gravity through mass-varying neutrino oscillations.

♻ ☆ Cosmological Correlators Using Tensor Networks

We develop tensor-network methods for computing cosmological correlators nonperturbatively in de Sitter space and use them to test the proposal that suitably defined in-in correlators can be obtained from an in-out formalism by gluing the expanding and contracting Poincaré patches. Focusing on interacting $1+1$-dimensional $φ^4$ theory, we formulate finite-time lattice observables using Matrix Product State (MPS) techniques and analyze the regulator subtleties associated with the singular behavior near the patching surface. We consider two different contour prescriptions: a finite-time real-contour and a complex contour which properly accounts for the regulator. In the regulated light-field theory, exact-diagonalization and MPS checks support recovery of the full complex in--in/in--out equality at the tested finite cutoffs, suggesting a non-perturbative resolution of light field singularities in perturbation theory. We briefly discuss how these methods extend to low-angular-momentum sectors in $3+1$ dimensions, and why regimes of rapid entanglement growth may eventually motivate quantum-computing implementations.

☆ Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
Vladimir Juričić, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido
Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds. Notably, the fractional part of this charge is insensitive to local perturbations of the dislocation core, and it therefore persists after the in-gap core state is removed, as we show analytically in the chain limit and numerically away from it. In the Weyl-semimetal counterpart, the response to a magnetic flux separates this crystalline charge from the charge set by the Chern number of each momentum slice. We propose that a half-integer core charge that persists after the in-gap peak disappears from the local spectrum can be detected in artificial electronic and optical lattices, with metamaterials providing complementary access to the core modes.

☆ Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
Jingye Tan, Benjamin A. Jasperson, Eric Rothchild, Anders Johansson, Rèmi Dingreville, Krishna Garikipati, Mitchell A. Wood
Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

☆ Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
Kian P. Abdolazizi, Kevin Linka, Christian J. Cyron
Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces. Pruning and symbolic regression then reduce the trained network to a compact closed-form strain energy that satisfies every constitutive requirement. On perforated natural-rubber membranes, the CKANs reproduce the DIC displacement fields with median errors between one and two percent, and transfer to a hole pattern withheld from training. On a perforated silicone plate, a CKAN trained on one stretch profile at a single load reproduces that profile and the measured reaction force to within a few percent. On an aortic specimen inflated under pressure, an anisotropic CKAN predicts the inflated three-dimensional shape. The discovered closed-form energies match the CKANs they replace on the training data and can be compared directly with established models.

The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available. In insulating NiO, restricted electronic scattering channels reduces the ultrafast response. Our results distinguish ultrafast demagnetization from exchange-enhanced precession and identify the interplay of spin-flip probability and electronic scattering rate as a key factor governing the nonequilibrium response of compensated magnets.

☆ Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
Jacqueline Hidalgo-Jiménez, Payam Edalati, Md Amirul Islam, Makoto Arita, Dmitry Chernyshov, Bidyut Baran Saha, Kaveh Edalati
This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

Ryotaro Okabe, Shoki Kishida, Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Dominic Bollettieri, Takuya Isogawa, Yongqiang Cheng, Mingda Li, Masaki Adachi
Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.

☆ Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
Asmund Ottesen, Shun Feng, Edoardo Lopriore, Yaroslav Zhumagulov, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Oleg V. Yazyev, Andras Kis
A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. Our optical probe reveals intermediate states of vertically aligned interfacial polarisation with magnitudes that confirm cumulative polarisation in multilayers. It must be stressed that the arrays of helices observed are distinct from moiré patterns; they facilitate lattice rotation combining plastic and elastic deformation and are not simply a superposition of lattices, twisted with respect to one another. However, key challenges remain such as the balance between imaging throughput and measurement accuracy, the extraction of multiple parameters with high confidence, and non-intrusive subsurface characterization, etc. This Review highlights recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-assistance in high-throughput data processing, visualizing interfacial thermal transport, and nonintrusive subsurface analysis, and offers outlooks for future research directions such as spectral mapping of heat carriers, three-dimensional property mapping, and AI-agentic experimental designs. In inference, a user-specified family template selects the source component for each atom-wise representation, enabling direct control over the family composition of generated crystals. Moreover, selected family templates increase the fraction of generated crystals predicted to be stable or metastable, demonstrating that latent-space composition control can support targeted exploration of promising chemical regions without additional optimization techniques such as reinforcement learning. Code is available at https://github.com/hhw11/FamilySpace

Consistent with these properties, nickel-rich cathode/lithium-metal anode full cells charge at 10C at room temperature and at 2C at $-40$ $^\circ$C. Residual trends for neutral or weakly localized defects are described by higher-order polynomial fits in $1/L^{3}$ and $1/L^{4}$. Hybrid-functional energetics corrected using PBE+U-based finite-size trends confirm the intrinsic $p-n$ doping character of Cu$_3$N under the conditions considered and demonstrate that no single finite-size correction can be transferred across all defect types.

Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

♻ ☆ Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite Qubit System
Dishaanth S. Pillai, G. M. Wysin
Quantum Computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement of quantum bits (qubits), to represent and manipulate information in multidimensional state spaces. This approach allows complex mathematical functions to be executed simultaneously rather than sequentially, making them much more efficient than classical computers. However, current quantum computers suffer from quantum decoherence, where small changes to their environment, such as thermal fluctuations and vibrations, affect the systems' fragile states. The goal of this study is to discuss the functionality of a proposed Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite qubit system by solving the unitary time-evolution of a quantum state vector for the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and traverse anisotropy terms at temperatures up to 10 K. The system can effectively transfer population between its two lowest states at rates predicted by the Rabi half-period, with 99.9% fidelity. Additionally, it can hold the population at a desired state without docohering. The results remained consistent for temperatures up to 10 K, meaning, unlike many common qubit systems, the proposed qubit system could function without a dilution fridge and is not fragile to thermal noise.

Second, the excessive doses typical of core-loss scattering can be alleviated using a Bayesian framework which, on a simulated Fe-doped strontium titanate, achieves nanometre to sub-nanometre depth precision from 100 to 1000 core-loss counts, depending on the signal-to-background.

We introduce an interpretable spectral attention-gating mechanism that reveals that the model autonomously learns to prioritize the orbital channels and energy windows most physically relevant to each target property. These results establish pDOS-augmented graph nodes as a broadly applicable strategy for infusing first-principles electronic-structure knowledge into graph networks, opening a practical route to high-accuracy property prediction in data-scarce regimes.

Furthermore, in the presence of Rashba spin--orbit coupling, we find an anomalous Josephson effect characterized by a finite equilibrium supercurrent at zero phase difference. Interestingly, despite the simultaneous breaking of time-reversal and inversion symmetries---conditions often associated with nonreciprocal superconducting transport---we do not observe a Josephson diode effect. Our results therefore highlight an important distinction between anomalous Josephson transport and superconducting nonreciprocity: the former does not necessarily imply a finite critical-current asymmetry between opposite current directions.

We present a randomized block Davidson-type eigensolver that replaces Euclidean orthogonalization with randomized Gram-Schmidt in a sketched inner product, requiring only a single pass over the basis while keeping its conditioning bounded independently of the input vectors. This modification changes only the Rayleigh-Ritz step, which becomes a definite generalized Hermitian eigenproblem. Ritz extraction remains exact, preserving true Ritz pairs and the interlacing property that makes each band energy an upper bound on the true one. The method is implemented in mixed precision for CPUs and GPUs from a single Julia code, interfaces matrix-free with DFTK, and is released in the open-source RandESC library. On sparse test problems with a fixed number of eigenpairs, the sketched solver overtakes its deterministic counterpart beyond matrix dimensions of about $2\times 10^4$ and is $25\%$ faster at $5\times 10^5$. In full self-consistent field DFT calculations, the benefits of sketching depend on the application case. With standard pseudopotentials and plane-wave cutoffs, efficiency gains are limited. As the number of requested states grows with system size, orthogonalization savings are offset by the generalized eigenproblem. However, some highly accurate pseudopotentals require larger cutoffs, and in this regime, the randomized solver is measurably better by $6\%$ overall. Its relative efficiency also improves as simulated systems get larger.

♻ ☆ Probing the limits of materials design via a comprehensive crystal database of 14.6 million structures with 140 properties

Forward screening and inverse design drive materials discovery, yet their limits remain unquantified because records of known crystal structures and properties are fragmented across databases. Consequently, forward screening leaves known crystals underexplored for new functions, whereas generative and autonomous discovery has repeatedly reported known phases or close variants as new materials. Here we match structures across 55 databases to assemble MateriaViva, a unified database of 14.6 million distinct crystals and over one billion property values. To provide the missing properties of every structure, a task we term property completion, we develop an equivariant Crystal Graph Transformer Network with state-of-the-art accuracy on nine benchmark tasks and apply 140 property-prediction models across the database. These predictions reveal the underestimated potential of forward screening, identifying tens of thousands of high-performance candidates among previously synthesized or computationally studied materials that lack recorded target-property values. Conversely, comparison with MateriaViva shows that the novelty of inverse design has been overestimated, as 55-100% of inverse-designed structures are not new. Under equal density functional theory verification budgets for bulk-modulus design, inverse design yields a higher fraction of qualifying candidates, whereas forward screening reaches the higher bulk modulus. MateriaViva thus provides a comprehensive reference for probing the limits of both paradigms, revealing unrecognized performance in known crystals and directing inverse design beyond reported structures.

Ground-state charge transfer injects holes into MoS2, which suppresses negative trion formation and enhances the radiative recombination of neutral excitons. In addition, resonant energy transfer, enabled by spectral overlap between PTCDA and MoS2, diverts excitation energy from PTCDA to MoS2. ♻ ☆ Disorder-free many-body localization in real quantum materials

The strong correlations among in-plane Ag atoms give rise to significant phononic flat bands and static two-dimensional off-center displacements of Ag atoms ranging from 0 to 0.5 angstrom with non-ergodic behavior. With a few representative materials, we prove that low-energy phononic flat bands serve as a promising indicator for a catalogue of DFMBL materials. As temperature rising, this static localization state with multiple degenerate local configurations persists up to near room temperature before transforming into a dynamically correlated state at a higher temperature. Emergent vibrational modes in the THz range and star-like topological structures constitute the low-energy excitation in the DFMBL phase. Moreover, the atomic engineering of a single Ag atom position induces a collective, correlated triangular motif, manifesting a generalized Winger solid in the atomic degree of freedom and underpinning the DFMBL regime. The identified DFMBL phase in a real material system offers a unified framework for understanding the rich quantum phenomena, such as the boson peak, the Debye-Einstein two-channel thermal conductivity and the spiral spin liquid state in quantum materials, and also offers a promising platform for topologically protected quantum computation and quantum memory.

☆ Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
Luisa Eck, Paul Fendley
The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

The (effective) string tension $σ$ at zero and finite- temperatures are compared between the theory with and without annealed charges. The quantity $T_c/\sqrtσ$ for the QLM with annealed charges is similar to the usual $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory, while the theory without the charges provides a new universal value.

At lower temperatures, two distant observers can estimate the shared direction of order more accurately. The maximum mutual information they can obtain by separate measurements grows logarithmically with the radius of their regions. The leading term is the same throughout each ordered phase, while the constant term $\mathcal{C}(T)=\tfrac12\ln[Υ(T)/T]+c_{\mathrm{geom}}$ is strictly larger at lower temperatures. Here $Υ(T)$ is the phase stiffness and $c_{\mathrm{geom}}$ depends only on the region geometry. A quasi-local channel cannot increase this constant, so it is invariant under two-way conversion. Cooling would increase it and is therefore impossible between any two distinct temperatures in the ordered phase. On finite lattices, cooling with vanishing error requires a circuit whose causal radius grows at least linearly with the lattice side length. The Pfaffian representation reveals a block Toeplitz--Hankel structure and allows us to extract the large-size scaling in several thermal regimes. We identify it with the normalized midpoint disorder-field one-point function of the free-boundary Ising CFT. ♻ ☆ Replica Fragmentation and Glassy Dynamics in Parity Learning

We study how independently trained Transformer neural networks reconstruct a binary string from its local domain walls. Runs sharing the data and training protocol can realize different functions. We treat them as replicas and measure truth alignment $m$, prediction confidence $q_{\mathrm{self}}$, and cross-replica agreement $q_{\mathrm{cross}}$. Confident disagreement defines the finite-size replica fragmentation that we call glass-like. With small training sets, replicas predict all training examples correctly but remain confident in incorrect predictions for unseen inputs, a regime we call memorization. With larger sets, runs can generalize and then retreat. Retreat occurs when outputs start to deviate from truth while confidence remains high. The frontier between learned and unlearned outputs recedes toward shorter strings. Many later recover as the frontier advances again. The self--cross gap $q_{\mathrm{self}}-q_{\mathrm{cross}}$ clearly distinguishes the three learning regimes of memorization, retreat, and recovery. With overall and position-dependent truth alignment subtracted, their residual correlations also differ: memorizing replicas have weakly and uniformly correlated residuals, while retreat has the largest fraction of replica pairs whose residuals are anti-correlated. That is, on the inputs where one replica of such a pair does better than its average, the other tends to do worse. These finite-size observations distinguish persistent memorization from ongoing retreat--recovery dynamics. The thermodynamic and long-time limits, and extensions to other learning tasks, remain open.

♻ ☆ Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning

We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(ρ_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.

In particular, Bog.~sc$GW$ systematically overestimates the correlation energy, with errors increasing rapidly as the attractive interaction strength grows. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $μ_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991, when the LEP and SLC precision data pointed toward supersymmetric unification, but it eventually gave way to renewed disappointment over the absence of superpartners and the sharpening of the LEP paradox. I also describe how the realization that Newtonian gravity had been tested only down to distances of order centimeters opened the door to large extra dimensions. Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry. I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

The $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-$ process provides excellent sensitivity to weak dipole operators through resonant $Z$ production and $Z$-pole energy scans, while $γγ\to τ^+τ^-$ yields the strongest constraint on the anomalous magnetic moment owing to the dominance of linear interference effects in the near-threshold region. Higher-energy stages improve the sensitivity to the $τ$ electric dipole moment. The radiative processes $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-γ$ and $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$ provide complementary, though subleading, probes of $τ$ dipole operators. Combining all channels, we estimate the statistical reach at the 95% CL to be $|Δa_τ|<2.8\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<2.5\times10^{-18}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<4.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, improving upon the current bounds by several orders of magnitude. These projections quantify the potential statistical reach of the FCC-ee program, motivating dedicated studies incorporating detector effects, systematic uncertainties, and higher-order theoretical predictions.

♻ ☆ Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at future lepton colliders
Dario Buttazzo, Gabriele Levati, Yang Ma, Fabio Maltoni, Paride Paradisi, ZeQiang Wang
The electric and magnetic dipole moments of the electron and of the muon provide stringent tests of the Standard Model and sensitive probes of new physics. By contrast, the corresponding dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton remain weakly constrained. This study explores the potential of future lepton colliders, focusing on the $e^+e^-$ Future Circular Collider and a multi-TeV muon collider, to probe $τ$ dipole moments. We consider multiple channels, including $\ell^+\ell^- \to τ^+τ^-$ ($\ell=e,μ$), associated Higgs production $μ^+μ^- \to τ^+τ^- H$, radiative Higgs decays $H \to τ^+τ^-γ$, and vector-boson scattering $\ell^+\ell^- \to \ell^+\ell^-τ^+τ^-$ and $μ^+μ^- \to \barνντ^+τ^-$. Our results show that these facilities are highly complementary and can extend existing bounds by several orders of magnitude.
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures; updated references to companion papers
♻ ☆ Transverse-momentum resummation effects on angular coefficients in Z and W boson hadroproduction
Stefano Camarda, Giancarlo Ferrera, Lorenzo Rossi, Gabriele Francesco Sala
We present a comprehensive analysis of the angular coefficients of $Z$ and $W$ boson production at hadron colliders in different kinematical ranges, using data from the ATLAS, LHCb, and CMS Collaborations at the LHC, including the recent CMS measurement at $\sqrt{s}=13$~TeV, as well as CDF data at the Tevatron. We provide theoretical predictions obtained by consistently combining the resummation of logarithmically enhanced QCD corrections at small transverse momentum $q_T$ up to next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy (NNLL) with the fixed-order calculation through $\mathcal{O}(α_S^2)$. The fixed-order helicity cross sections entering the finite component are evaluated using the new complete analytic NLO calculation implemented in the DYTurbo program. This implementation makes it possible to obtain fast and numerically stable predictions for all the angular coefficients and to perform an extensive study of their theoretical uncertainties. We quantify the impact of transverse-momentum resummation on the angular coefficients and we estimate the associated theoretical uncertainties, including scale variations, parton distribution functions, non-perturbative effects, the treatment of the transition region and the recoil prescription used to generate the lepton angular distribution of the resummed component. Within the estimated theoretical uncertainties, resummation improves the description of several measurements, particularly for $A_2$, while its impact on $A_0$ depends more strongly on the dataset and on the theoretical choices. The Lam--Tung combination $A_0-A_2$ is essentially unaffected by resummation.

♻ ☆ Exploring enhanced non-resonant di-Higgs production at the HL-LHC with neural networks
Leandro Da Rold, Manuel Epele, Anibal D. Medina, Nicolás I. Mileo, Alejandro Szynkman
We investigate di-Higgs production in the $b\bar{b}γγ$ final state at the LHC, focusing on scenarios where the gluon fusion process is enhanced by new colored scalars, which could be identified as squarks or leptoquarks. We consider two benchmarks characterized by the mass of the lightest colored scalar, BM$_{\mathrm{L}}$ and BM$_{\mathrm{H}}$, corresponding to 464 GeV and 621 GeV, respectively. Using Monte Carlo simulations for both the signal and the dominant backgrounds, we perform a discovery analysis with deep neural networks, exploring various architectures and input variables. Our results show that the discrimination power is maximized by employing two dedicated classifiers, one trained against QCD backgrounds and another against backgrounds involving single-Higgs processes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that including high-level features -- such as the invariant masses $m_{γγ}$, $m_{bb}$, and $m_{hh}$, as well as the transverse momenta and angular separations of the photon and $b$-jet pairs -- significantly improves the performance compared to using only low-level features as the invariant mass and momenta of the final particles. For the latter case, we find that architectures processing photon and $b$-jet variables separately can enhance the significance for BM$_{\mathrm{H}}$. Projecting for an integrated luminosity of 3 ab$^{-1}$, we obtain a significance of 7.2 for BM$_{\mathrm{L}}$, while it drops to 3.1 for BM$_{\mathrm{H}}$. In the particular case of BM$_{\mathrm{L}}$, discovery level significance can be reached at 1.4 ab$^{-1}$. We also estimate how these results could be modified by potential systematic uncertainties.

♻ ☆ Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
Mateus Reinke Pelicer, Nikolas Cruz-Camacho, Rajesh Kumar, Veronica Dexheimer, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler
We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $μ_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $μ_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $Δ$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $Ξ^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $μ_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

♻ ☆ Lattice QCD study of the $K^*(892)$ resonance at the physical point
Qu-Zhi Li, Chuan Liu, Liuming Liu, Peng Sun, Jia-Jun Wu, Zhiguang Xiao, Yi-Bo Yang, Han-Qing Zheng
We present a lattice QCD study of the $K^*(892)$ resonance using eight $N_f=2+1$ Wilson-Clover ensembles with three lattice spacings and six pion masses ranging from 135 to 320 MeV. For each ensemble, a large number of finite volume energy levels in the $P$-wave $Kπ$ channel are determined. The energy dependence of the scattering phase shift is then obtained from Lüscher's finite-volume method. To systematically assess parametrization dependence, the amplitude is described using three different models, which yield consistent results. The resulting phase shifts show a clear resonant behavior for all ensembles, and the corresponding $K^*(892)$ resonance pole is identified on the second Riemann sheet in the complex energy plane. The pole positions are extrapolated to the physical pion mass and the continuum limit, yielding a $K^*(892)$ resonance located at $\sqrt{s_0} = [882.10\binom{+7.36}{-10.29} (0.30) -i22.73(3.32)(0.63)] \mathrm{MeV}$, which is in excellent agreement with the experimental value. The quoted uncertainty includes the statistical uncertainty and systematic uncertainties associated with the choice of fit windows and three parameterizations of the scattering amplitude.

♻ ☆ Untangling the Integration-By-Parts Equations
Junhan W. Liu, Alexander Mitov
In this work, we present an algorithm which converts the Integration-by-Parts (IBP) equations into single-variable recurrence relations. We refer to this procedure as {\it diagonalization}. Diagonalized IBP equations are indispensable for reducing loop integrals with extremely high numerator powers to master integrals, and for solving IBP identities in closed analytic form. A prime example is provided by multivariate Mellin representations of loop amplitudes and cross sections. The extension of these methods to other multivariate recurrence relations is also discussed. As a by-product of our diagonalization procedure, we show how the IBP equations can be cast into an efficient, fully triangular form that is well suited for computer implementation. Several complicated topologies have been computed.
comment: 15 pages, 5 figures, results attached
♻ ☆ Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
Keita Horie, Rin Kagami, Chiho Nonaka
Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

♻ ☆ Geometric algebra as the input language of collider foundation models
E. Abasov, L. Dudko, F. Grigoryev, P. Volkov, A. Zaborenko
We describe a hard hadron-collider event as a single geometric object. Each reconstructed final-state object is a multivector of $\Cl(1,3)\otimes\Vflav$ that combines its four-momentum with its object-type label. The event multivector $\evMV$ is the direct sum of these per-object multivectors. Products in the algebra generate the higher grades from the measured four-momenta. The grades organise nearly every observable in current use, from invariants at grade zero to decay-plane bivectors, oriented three-volumes and the CP-odd pseudoscalar at grades two to four. The high-level invariants and the low-level four-momentum recipe of earlier analyses, and the inputs of equivariant networks, are recovered as projections onto specific grades. We give a per-grade dictionary of $32$ classical observables and an inventory of the symmetries acting on $\evMV$. A theorem extending the Cayley--Menger identity to Minkowski space shows that the higher grades give no Lorentz invariant beyond $\{p_i\!\cdot\!p_j,\,m_i^2\}$ except the CP-odd sign of the pseudoscalar. Grades two and three n evertheless describe the decay planes and decay volumes of the event compactly, as covariant objects. The representation is intended as a uniform input layer for foundation models of collider physics. As a simple example of its use, we apply it to the resonance-topology separation of $pp\!\to\!tWb$ with a small Lorentz-equivariant multivector transformer of L-GATr type. In an ablation over eight input representations of this example, the classifier improves when a fixed reference bivector encoding the beam plane, which the momenta do not contain, is added to the input.

♻ ☆ Soft Scale Symmetry Breaking with Laguerre Explicit Regulators
A. R. Vieira
In this work, we search for explicit regulators that do not spuriously break scale invariance starting from conditions established by implicit regularization. There is a family of regulator functions that obeys the conditions and leads to soft breaking terms of the dilatation current. This family of functions is shown to be related to the Laguerre polynomials. We apply this approach by revisiting quadratic divergences in the context of the naturalness problem of the Standard Model and show that the quadratic dependence of the Higgs mass on the cutoff is not required by consistency of scale-symmetry breaking and can be removed within this class of regulators. Applications of these regulators beyond 1-loop order are also considered.
comment: 21 pages, 7 figures
♻ ☆ Strongly supercooled first-order phase transitions: monopole abundance, entropy production and homogeneity consistency
Chen Zhang, Yue Niu, Xin Zhang
We investigate whether monopole production in the early universe from a first-order phase transition in a unified gauge theory can be significantly suppressed if the phase transition is subject to strong supercooling but still completes successfully. This is facilitated by adopting a Gaussian nucleation model and assuming the false vacuum energy released is transferred to sectors which behave effectively as radiation in terms of cosmological evolution. We distinguish three criteria of phase-transition completion: the comoving measure completion (CMC) characterized by the eventual vanishing of the false-vacuum fraction (FVF), the physical volume completion (PVC) characterized by the eventual vanishing of the physical volume of false vacuum, and the asymptotic thermodynamic completion (ATC), which refers to the finiteness of total entropy production. Assuming an idealized Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology, it is shown that the three criteria share exactly the same completion boundary, away from which they are completely equivalent. It is further shown that monopole abundance can be arbitrarily suppressed for parameter points approaching the completion boundary from the successful side. Nevertheless, for parameter points too close to the completion boundary, justification of the self-consistency of a homogeneous FLRW cosmology is difficult. We propose the use of the Hubble-scale FVF root-mean-square fluctuation to diagnose the homogeneity consistency issue, and find that arbitrarily strong suppression of monopole abundance relative to a reasonable Kibble estimate is not justifiable in terms of homogeneity consistency. These findings also have implications for gravitational wave production in strongly supercooled phase transitions.
comment: 20 pages including Supplementary Material, 2 figures; references added
♻ ☆ Estimation of the cumulant $b_4$ and sextic self-coupling of the QCD axion at finite temperature and density
Xinguang Li, Zhao Zhang
The sixth-order cumulant $b_4$ of the QCD topological charge distribution and the axion's sextic self-coupling at finite temperature $T$ and baryon chemical potential $μ$ are calculated within the two-flavor quark-meson (QM) model without and with the Polyakov-loop dynamics. The $b_4$ in the vacuum falls within the range predicted by lattice SU(3) pure-gauge simulations, and at large $T$ and/or $μ$, it tends to a constant predicted by the dilute instanton gas approximation. Both $b_4$ and the axion's sextic self-coupling diverge at the QCD critical point and flip sign across the phase transition. The range of accuracy of the fourth- and sixth-order Taylor expansions of the free energy as a function of the $θ$ parameter is investigated via comparison with the full potential at the mean-field level.
comment: 17 pages, 17 figures, references added; accepted version to appear in Phys. Rev. D
♻ ☆ Spin-dependent fermion potentials from mixed tensor couplings of massive spin-1 and spin-2 bosons
D. Khadka, V. V. Flambaum
Searches for weak spin-dependent forces are commonly interpreted in terms of a basis of sixteen rotationally invariant two-fermion potentials. We derive finite-range coordinate-space potentials generated by a massive spin-1 boson with vector, axial-vector, tensor, and pseudotensor couplings to Dirac fermions. In addition to the familiar vector--vector, vector--axial-vector, and axial-vector--axial-vector interactions, we obtain the mixed vector--tensor, vector--pseudotensor, axial-vector--tensor, and axial-vector--pseudotensor potentials, together with tensor--tensor, tensor--pseudotensor, and pseudotensor--pseudotensor terms. We retain the contact terms needed in atomic-scale applications and give compact expressions that include both orderings of inequivalent fermion vertices. We then extend the analysis to a massive spin-2 mediator described by a symmetric Fierz--Pauli field. Besides the conventional coupling to the conserved fermion energy--momentum tensor, we consider a symmetric axial-tensor current. Its nonconservation for massive fermions makes the longitudinal spin-2 helicities contribute to axial-tensor--axial-tensor exchange. The leading minimal spin-2 interactions are either P,T even or P odd and T evenl. Heavy-mediator contact limits and the distinction between the M-->0 massive-spin-2 limit and a genuine massless graviton are also discussed. We map the resulting interactions onto the sixteen-potential Dobrescu--Mocioiu basis and use this mapping to translate existing experimental constraints into numerical limits on spin-1 and spin-2 coupling products in the small- and large-mediator-mass regimes, together with representative limits at finite mediator masses. The derived relations between the boson-exchange coupling constants and the coefficients of the basis potentials also allow published exclusion curves to be rescaled to arbitrary mediator masses.
♻ ☆ Particle accelerators as a path to intergovernmental collaboration: the case of the first electron positron collider and the power of theoretical physics
Giulia Pancheri
I revisit the history of the first matter-antimatter collider built in Italy in 1960 and carried to success through an inter-European collaboration with France, to underline the need for large intergovernmental efforts in the realization of particle accelerators such as the proposed electron synchrotron in the Greater Caribbean region. The foundational role of the Austrian born theoretical physicist Bruno Touschek and his life path through Europe before and after World War II is briefly recalled. The role of CERN as a post-war intergovernmental institution in jump-starting the international collaboration between the Frascati National Laboratories in Italy and the Laboratoire de l'Accelerateur Lineaire d'Orsay in France is highlighted through historical documents, and contributions from interviews with the protagonists of Touschek's game-changing proposal.
comment: First version with 10 pages, 5 figures, new version 14 pages with 21 images in 7 figures, corrected typos, added text and a new section with interviews, added references and figures to clarify and provide additional proofs to argument of intergovernmental collaboration, text inspired by presentation at 2025 Colloque Haissinski, IJCLab, Orsay, France
♻ ☆ Enhancement of Weak Interactions in Phase Transitions in Condensed Matter and Early Universe
V. V. Flambaum
Parity-violating weak interactions produce extremely small energy differences between left- and right-handed chiral systems. We show that these microscopic effects may be amplified during collective phenomena such as phase transitions. The enhancement factor is proportional to the critical number of atoms, $N_c$, in the nucleus of the new phase. Measurement of the ratio of produced left- and right-handed chiral structures may provide a way to determine $N_c$. Experiments in which spin-chiral structures are formed in ZnCr$_2$Se$_4$ during a phase transition in crossed electric and magnetic fields indicate an effective amplification corresponding to $N_c\sim 10^9-10^{10}$. We emphasize, however, that such large values cannot be inferred from homogeneous capillary nucleation alone, since the same parameters imply a very large nucleation barrier; in real crystals heterogeneous nucleation, defects, strain, and domain-growth dynamics may be essential. We also discuss, more cautiously, whether analogous collective enhancement could operate in first-order cosmological phase transitions beyond the Standard Model. The Standard-Model electroweak transition for the observed Higgs mass is a crossover and therefore has no critical bubble nucleus.
♻ ☆ Asymmetric dark matter from leptogenesis in type-III seesaw framework with modular $S_4$ symmetry
Abhishek, V. Suryanarayana Mummidi
We present a unified framework for neutrino masses, baryogenesis, and dark matter based on a modular $S_4$ symmetry combined with a type-III seesaw mechanism. All Yukawa couplings, CP phases, and flavor textures originate from a single complex modulus $τ$, whose vacuum expectation value controls both visible and dark sector dynamics. The same modular parameter fixes the neutrino mass matrix, determines the CP asymmetries driving resonant leptogenesis, and correlates the resulting baryon and dark matter abundances. A detailed numerical analysis shows that the model reproduces all neutrino oscillation data within the $3σ$ NuFIT~5.2 (2024) ranges for normal ordering, predicting $δ_{\rm CP} \simeq \pm (150^\circ-180^\circ)$, $\sum m_ν\simeq(0.06-0.08)~\mathrm{eV}$, and an effective Majorana mass $m_{ββ} \simeq (0.3 - 4)\times 10^{-3}~\mathrm{eV}$, testable in next-generation neutrinoless double-beta decay experiments. The same modular Yukawas yield resonantly enhanced CP asymmetries $|ε_{L,χ}| \sim 10^{-9}-10^{-6}$ at $M_Σ\sim 10^{7}~\mathrm{GeV}$, successfully generating the observed baryon asymmetry $η_B\simeq6\times10^{-10}$ and dark relic density $Ω_χh^2\simeq0.12$ without additional free parameters. The predicted correlation $Ω_χ/Ω_B\simeq5.4$ fixes the dark matter mass to $m_χ\simeq0.1-2~\mathrm{GeV}$, consistent with all current constraints. This framework therefore realizes a fully predictive baryon$-$dark matter co-genesis, where the geometry of the modular symmetry links the origin of flavor, CP violation, and the cosmic matter asymmetry.
comment: Published version, 29 pages, 12 figures
♻ ☆ Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
Yang Yu, Lei Feng
Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $3.1\times10^{-43}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $α\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures
♻ ☆ Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
Sergey Troitsky
Selected astrophysical methods for testing particle-physics models are reviewed. Stellar structure and evolution constrain additional channels of energy loss and transport; high-energy photon propagation probes photon mixing with new particles and modifications of electron-positron pair production; large-volume neutrino telescopes are used to search for magnetic monopoles, neutrinos from superheavy dark-matter decay, and non-standard neutrino propagation. Recent applications of these methods are discussed, involving the tip of the red-giant branch in the color-luminosity diagram, gamma-ray burst 221009A, and data from the Baikal Gigaton Volume Detector (Baikal-GVD) and the IceCube experiment. In each case, particle-physics parameters are inferred through a forward model that accounts for the response to new physics, propagation, detection, and nuisance parameters.

♻ ☆ Radiative Dirac Neutrino Masses from Modular $S_3$ Symmetry in an Axion Model
Sin Kyu Kang, Ranjeet Kumar, Hiroshi Okada
We present a unified axion model framework that simultaneously addresses the origin of neutrino masses, leptonic flavor structure, the strong CP problem, and dark matter. The model is based on a global $U(1)_{\rm PQ}$ symmetry combined with a modular $S_3$ symmetry and is realized within a novel class of KSVZ-type axion model. Exotic colored fermions and scalars mediate radiative neutrino mass generation at the one loop-level. The PQ charge assignment forbids tree-level neutrino masses and leaves a residual $Z_3$ symmetry that ensures the Dirac nature of neutrinos. In the minimal realization, the neutrino mass matrix is of rank two, predicting one massless neutrino. Consequently, the sum of neutrino masses is constrained for both the normal and inverted hierarchies. We analyze the implications for charged lepton flavor violation and the lepton $g-2$. The axion emerging from this framework dynamically resolves the strong CP problem and accounts for the observed dark matter abundance. Notably, the predicted axion-photon coupling is within reach of upcoming experiments and consistent with existing astrophysical and cosmological bounds.

♻ ☆ Dark Matter-Dark Radiation Interactions and the Hubble Tension
Manuel A. Buen-Abad, Zackaria Chacko, Ina Flood, Can Kilic, Gustavo Marques-Tavares, Taewook Youn
Models in which a subcomponent of dark matter interacts with dark radiation have been proposed as a solution to the Hubble tension. In this framework, the interacting subcomponent of dark matter is in thermal equilibrium with the dark radiation in the early universe, but decouples from it around the time of matter-radiation equality. We study this general class of models and evaluate the quality of fit to recent cosmological data on the cosmic microwave background (from Planck 2018 and ACT DR6), baryon acoustic oscillations, large-scale structure, supernovae type Ia, and Cepheid variables. We focus on three benchmark scenarios that differ in the rate at which the dark matter decouples from the dark radiation, resulting in different patterns of dark acoustic oscillations. Fitting without ACT DR6 data, we find that all three scenarios significantly reduce the Hubble tension relative to $Λ$CDM, with an exponentially fast decoupling being the most preferred. The tension is reduced to less than $2 \, σ$ in fits that don't include the SH0ES collaboration results as part of the data and to less than $1 \, σ$ when these are included. The preference for the interacting model is substantially reduced when ACT DR6 data are included. We find that the largest $H_0$ value at the $95 \%$ confidence region is $70.1$ km/s/Mpc without the SH0ES data, leading to only a mild reduction in the tension. This increases to $72.5$ km/s/Mpc, corresponding to a reduction in the tension to less than $3 \, σ$, if the SH0ES results are included in the fit.

♻ ☆ Atomic Dark Matter, Interacting Dark Radiation, and the Hubble Tension
Manuel A. Buen-Abad, Zackaria Chacko, Ina Flood, Can Kilic, Gustavo Marques-Tavares, Taewook Youn
We present a new class of interacting dark sector models that can address the Hubble tension. Interacting dark radiation (DR) has previously been put forward as a solution to the problem, but this proposal is disfavored by the high-$\ell$ cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. We modify this basic framework by introducing a subcomponent of dark matter (DM) that interacts strongly with the DR, so that together they constitute a tightly coupled fluid at early times. We show that if this subcomponent decouples from the interacting DR during the CMB epoch, the $\ell$ modes of the CMB that entered the horizon before decoupling are impacted differently from those that entered after, allowing a solution to the problem. We present a model that realizes this framework, which we dub "New Atomic Dark Matter", or nuADaM, in which the interacting dark matter (iDM) subcomponent is composed of dark atoms, and dark "neutrinos" with long-range interactions contribute to the DR, hence the name of the model. This iDM subcomponent is acoustic at early times but decouples from the DR following dark recombination. In contrast to conventional atomic dark matter (ADM) models, the dark photon is part of a richer DR sector, which ensures that it continues to be self-interacting even after recombination. We show that this model admits a significantly larger value of $H_0$ than $Λ\mathrm{CDM}$ when fit to CMB and BAO data, while maintaining a comparable goodness of fit. Once the SHOES data set is included, it provides a significantly better fit than $Λ\mathrm{CDM}$.
