♻ ☆ Accelerating systems as probes of Lorentz violation
Quentin G. Bailey, Nils A. Nilsson, Sawyer J. Star
We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for Lorentz violation. The dispersion relation, Hamiltonian, and massless and massive Wightman functions are obtained. We determine the conditions under which the scalar dynamics preserves boost symmetry and distinguish these from the weaker conditions required for stationarity along a single accelerated worldline. The Wightman functions are used to construct the finite-time Unruh-DeWitt response for a uniformly accelerated detector. For generic coefficients the response is nonstationary and depends on both the duration and temporal location of the measurement. The spectrum, which is the resulting excitation rate as a function of the energy level difference in the detector, is obtained numerically. It shows discernable differences with the usual massive thermal spectrum for dimensionless coefficients on the order of $10^{-7}$. Experimental implications of the result are discussed. As an alternative viewpoint, we place Lorentz violation in the point-particle sector, derive the exact trajectory generated by a constant electric field, and study the proper-time Fourier response of a conventional scalar wave along the modified trajectory.

♻ ☆ Assessing the enrichment of heat-producing elements in deep-mantle structures using a directional geoneutrino detector
Zhihao Xu, Misaki Hosoya, William F. McDonough, Taichi Sakai, Hiroko Watanabe
Determining the spatial distribution of heat-producing elements (HPEs) within the Earth is critical for understanding the planet's thermal and chemical evolution. A central debate is whether domains in the deep mantle, particularly the Large Low-Velocity Provinces (LLVP), represent anomalous, radiogenically enriched reservoirs. Variation in the surface flux of geoneutrinos provide a direct probe of Earth's internal radioactivity. However, current continental located detectors measure only the angle-integrated flux, leading to strong spatial trade-offs that substantially limit the ability of practical networks to uniquely resolve mantle compositional heterogeneity. This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster. I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991, when the LEP and SLC precision data pointed toward supersymmetric unification, but it eventually gave way to renewed disappointment over the absence of superpartners and the sharpening of the LEP paradox. I also describe how the realization that Newtonian gravity had been tested only down to distances of order centimeters opened the door to large extra dimensions. Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry. I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

♻ ☆ Runaway entanglement between a semiclassical background and parametrically-enhanced quantum fluctuations
Roxane Thériault, George Zahariade
We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Title changed for the published version
♻ ☆ Inaccessibility of the Schwarzschild Singularity to Quantum Probes
Vishnulal Cheriyodathillathu, Tanmay Patil, Saurya Das, Soumen Basak
We revisit the Schwarzschild singularity in a semiclassical setting where the background geometry is classical and quantum effects enter through Bohmian (quantal) trajectories associated with a Klein-Gordon wave function. Using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of the Klein-Gordon wavefunction, we show that the quantum-modified motion is equivalent to geodesic motion in an effective metric conformally related to Schwarzschild, with a conformal factor fixed by the wavefunction amplitude. Solving the wavefunction equation near $r\to 0$ determines this factor and yields finite curvature invariants, in suitable coordinates the interior extends smoothly and the effective spacetime is geodesically complete. Our result suggests that quantum probes on a prescribed classical background can experience an operationally regular effective geometry, even though the underlying Schwarzschild spacetime itself remains classically singular.
comment: 9 pages, Published version in Physics Letters B
♻ ☆ Fermionic Casimir memory from an anisotropic gravitational pulse
Celio R. Muniz, Herondy F. Santana Mota
We investigate the late-time energy deposited by a weak, spatially homogeneous anisotropic gravitational pulse in a massless Dirac field confined between two static parallel plates. The field satisfies MIT bag boundary conditions, while the prescribed geometry approaches Minkowski spacetime in both asymptotic time regions. Using a tetrad formulation, we show that the linear spin-connection contribution cancels for the traceless anisotropy, leaving a coupling to the shear component of the Dirac stress tensor. The pulse produces real fermion--antifermion pairs, whose deposited energy is evaluated through the corresponding Bogoliubov coefficients. Subtracting the production in unbounded space isolates a finite boundary-dependent contribution governed by the pulse duration relative to the characteristic spectral timescale set by the MIT gap. This contribution is negative in the adiabatic regime, where confinement suppresses excitations relative to the continuous free spectrum, and approaches zero from above in the impulsive limit. The late-time force on the plates is obtained separately from the normal stress $T^{zz}$ of the produced pairs, evaluated at fixed occupation numbers, with the field and the pulse present on both sides of each plate. The resulting pressure correction is the difference between the interior and exterior normal stresses. It reinforces the attractive Casimir force for both slow and fast pulses and reduces it in an intermediate window, so that it exhibits two sign changes. Unlike the bosonic vacuum-polarization memory previously obtained for the same class of backgrounds, the present effect is a dissipative fermionic memory carried by gravitationally created pairs. Here, memory denotes the persistent late-time modification of the quantum state after the pulse has vanished.
comment: 16 pages, 1 figure. Accepted in EPJC
♻ ☆ Multi-Centered Black Hole Index from a Superconformal Quiver Index
Canberk Sanli
We formulate a $D(2,1;0)$ superconformal index for scaling quiver quantum mechanics in its gauged sigma model description which preserves the hyperKähler with torsion geometry. These quivers describe the Coulomb-branch dynamics of multi-centered D-brane configurations in the $AdS_2$ scaling limit of type II Calabi--Yau compactifications. Using supersymmetric localization, we derive a fixed-point formula for this superconformal quiver index and identify the geometric origin of its saddle equations and fixed-point contributions. We compare the result with the configurational index of multi-centered BPS black holes, finding the same universal denominator and angular momentum weights but different saddle equations. We then examine the additional scaling contributions to the microscopic quiver index and show that, for the symmetric three-center cyclic family, the unequal-sign scaling term is exactly reproduced by the superconformal index.

♻ ☆ Untangling the Integration-By-Parts Equations
Junhan W. Liu, Alexander Mitov
In this work, we present an algorithm which converts the Integration-by-Parts (IBP) equations into single-variable recurrence relations. We refer to this procedure as {\it diagonalization}. Diagonalized IBP equations are indispensable for reducing loop integrals with extremely high numerator powers to master integrals, and for solving IBP identities in closed analytic form. A prime example is provided by multivariate Mellin representations of loop amplitudes and cross sections. The extension of these methods to other multivariate recurrence relations is also discussed. As a by-product of our diagonalization procedure, we show how the IBP equations can be cast into an efficient, fully triangular form that is well suited for computer implementation. Several complicated topologies have been computed.

♻ ☆ Edge observables in Maxwell theory on null boundaries
Dušan Đorđević, Olivera Miskovic, Antonia Montecinos, Tatjana Vukašinac
We study edge observables in three-dimensional Maxwell theory on null boundaries using a Hamiltonian formulation adapted to null foliations. We consider three backgrounds: Minkowski spacetime, the BTZ black hole, and de Sitter space, where the relevant boundaries are, respectively, null infinity, the black hole horizon, and the cosmological horizon. In all three cases we find, besides the usual $\mathrm U(1)$ charge, a second edge observable associated with a shift transformation intrinsic to the null boundary. The two charges are well defined quasilocally. They form a centrally extended algebra which, in Fourier modes, becomes two independent Abelian Kac--Moody algebras with opposite levels. Thus, the same centrally extended edge structure appears at both asymptotic and finite distance null boundaries. The phase space also admits charge-conjugation twisted configurations, in which the modes of the algebra are half-integer. Finally, in Minkowski spacetime we find an exact radiative solution in this twisted sector, with both charges nonvanishing.

♻ ☆ Algebraic traversable wormholes
Eyoab Bahiru
We discuss a large $N$ limit for the thermofield double state which at the extreme ($N=\infty$) limit is dual in the bulk to a back-reacted traversable wormhole, by making use of an operator in the algebra at infinity, an algebra familiar in the literature from the study of quasi-local algebras. We also compute, from a purely algebraic perspective, the effects registered by a left universe observer due to a unitary fluctuation on the right universe of the traversable wormhole, and reproduce a result from an earlier computation by Maldacena, Stanford and Yang \cite{Maldacena:2017axo}.

♻ ☆ Cohomological Aspects of Entanglement Entropy: From Information Theory to Noncommutative Geometry
R. C. Rashkov
We develop a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy that unifies information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry. Entropy is a 1-cocycle in information cohomology; we generalize this to the quantum setting via Hochschild and cyclic cohomology. For an inclusion of von Neumann algebras N contained in M with a faithful normal state w admitting a cyclic and separating vector, and a conditional expectation E: M -> N (whose existence is equivalent to modular invariance of N by Takesaki's theorem), we construct the entanglement complex as the image of the transgression map tau_w on the relative cyclic complex, where A is a dense *-subalgebra of M and B = A intersect N. Our main result identifies entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map HC*(A) -> HC*(B), up to the connecting homomorphism d of the long exact sequence of the pair (A,B); when d = 0, the identification is exact. The relative modular cocycle u_t = (Dw : D(w|_N) o E)_t generates explicit entanglement classes when E is not w-invariant, with the Araki relative entropy as its infinitesimal generator. The framework accommodates Type III von Neumann algebras, where no local density matrix exists, and leads to a holographic proposal: a subspace of H^1_ent is conjecturally dual to linearized modular Hamiltonian perturbations of the bulk entanglement wedge. We verify the construction in finite-dimensional, type II_1, and type III_1 examples.

♻ ☆ Soft Scale Symmetry Breaking with Laguerre Explicit Regulators
A. R. Vieira
In this work, we search for explicit regulators that do not spuriously break scale invariance starting from conditions established by implicit regularization. There is a family of regulator functions that obeys the conditions and leads to soft breaking terms of the dilatation current. This family of functions is shown to be related to the Laguerre polynomials. We apply this approach by revisiting quadratic divergences in the context of the naturalness problem of the Standard Model and show that the quadratic dependence of the Higgs mass on the cutoff is not required by consistency of scale-symmetry breaking and can be removed within this class of regulators. Applications of these regulators beyond 1-loop order are also considered.

♻ ☆ Quantum information spreading via higher-order operator correlators
M Süzen
We provide an exact analytical benchmarks into measuring the quantum information spreading by introducing N-operator correlators. Leveraging the idea from N-point correlation function from cosmology, we formulate a generalized Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlator (OTOC), called N-Operator Correlator (NOC). Such formulation can reduce the effect of restricted analysis associated with selecting only two operators for OTOC. NOC can take into account a larger set of measurement probes in measuring the degree of quantum information spreading. We demonstrate these concepts with two analytically tractable systems with computing thermal averages of operator time evolutions at a finite temperature: a single qubit in longitudinal field and isotropic XXX model with a transverse field, two-qubit system. Our analytical benchmark serves as a basic introduction to generalized operator correlators in quantum mechanics.

In this version, updates on Pauli bases and simpler probe combination choice, a new short section on n-point and n-probe OTOC review, the symbolic workflow is available on request on Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24339371
♻ ☆ An ode to instantons
Oliver Janssen, Joel Karlsson, Flavio Riccardi, Mattia Varrone
We review a formalism for semiclassical time evolution in quantum mechanics, identifying complex saddle points in real time, real saddle points in complex time, and complex saddle points in complex time that reproduce known answers to classic problems. For the decay of a metastable state, we find finite-time and finite-energy analogs of the "bounce" which have no zero or negative modes. The one-loop phase of the wave function and the multiplicity of bounce solutions at late times are discussed. The motivation for this work is to learn how to compute decay rates in quantum field theory in situations with interesting time dependence, by first taking a humble step back to the fascinating world of quantum mechanics.

♻ ☆ General Lagrangian formulations for mixed-antisymmetric tensor fields on flat backgrounds
Alexander A. Reshetnyak
We present, for the first time, local Lagrangian formulations for (ir)reducible integer higher-spin massless and massive Poincare group representations subject to Young tableau with $k$ columns $Y[\hat{s}_1,\hat{s}_2,...,\hat{s}_k]$ in $d$-dimensional Minkowski space-time. The particles are described in a metric-like formulation by tensor fields carrying $k$ groups of antisymmetric Lorentz indices $Φ_{μ^1[{\hat{s}_1}],μ^2[{\hat{s}_2}],..., μ^k[{\hat{s}_k}]}$ using the BRST procedure with both the complete operator $Q$ and incomplete $Q_c$ BRST operators. Starting from a description of bosonic mixed-antisymmetric higher-spin fields in terms of an auxiliary Fock space associated with a special Poincare module, we realize a conversion of the initial operator constraint system into a system of first-class operator constraints. For this purpose, we find, for the first time, by means of Verma module the auxiliary representations of the constraint subalgebra, to be isomorphic due to Howe duality to $so(k,k)$ algebra, and containing the subsystem of second-class operators in terms of new oscillator variables forming the Fock module. An unconstrained (with $Q$) and constrained (with $Q_c$ and BRST invariant algebraic constraints) gauge Lagrangian formulations with equivalent dynamics, but different configuration spaces are found. We outline within $Q_c$-approach the concept of consistent local cubic interactions and evaluate the candidate structure of cubic vertices involving $p\geq 3$ copies of interacting massless mixed-antisymmetric fields.

♻ ☆ Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
Yu-Qi Chen, Hai-Shan Liu, H. Lu
We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.
♻ ☆ Textured phase diagrams of featureless insulators
Sashank Singam, Nick G. Jones, Abhishodh Prakash
We study phase diagrams of charge-conserving `class A' non-interacting fermions, focusing on the trivial phase in various dimensions. Such phases are usually termed `featureless' to distinguish them from those others with either symmetry-broken or topological order. We show that the presence of non-trivial topological families of states, including charge pumps and their generalizations, results in phase diagrams being endowed with non-trivial topological textures that can be visualized through Berry phases and their higher-dimensional generalizations. We show that for non-interacting fermion systems with translation invariance, these `higher' Berry phases can be computed using integrals of non-abelian Chern-Simons forms of the Berry-Bloch connection over momentum and parameter spaces. Singularities in these textures correspond to gap-closing loci of `diabolical points', which represent the obstruction to contracting topologically non-trivial families of states, and bulk-boundary correspondence results in a locus of robust boundary modes that terminate at the bulk diabolical points. In the presence of finite chemical potential, we argue that the edge modes are generically robust without any need for fine-tuning for two and higher dimensions, whereas in one dimension they are `estranged' in the phase diagram, i.e. appearing at different parameter values for different edges. We demonstrate our results by constructing several microscopic models of non-interacting fermions. We argue stability to interactions and explore proximate phase diagrams by mapping to continuum field theories.

♻ ☆ On-shell renormalization of sine-Gordon by the quantum inverse scattering method
Francesco Beccarini, Claudio Conti
In the quantum inverse scattering method the sine-Gordon model is solved on a lattice. Sklyanin, Takhtajan and Faddeev observed that the continuum and infinite-volume limits of the vacuum quasiparticle density become uniform only after the length of the box is rescaled, which absorbs the dependence on the cut-off up to a finite ambiguity in the mass scale. We develop this obser- vation into a renormalization of the spectrum internal to the method: since all the eigenvalues of the monodromy operator depend on the lattice only through the vacuum density, the uniform limit removes the cut-off, and an on-shell condition on the lightest breather fixes the remaining ambiguity. We show explicitly that the results coincide with those of normal ordering and of conformal perturbation theory: the dependence on the cut-off is the multiplicative renormaliza- tion of the cosine, with the exponent fixed by its scaling dimension, the masses scale with the bare coupling with the same power, and the spectrum agrees with the semiclassical one and with the exact S-matrix. Since the procedure requires neither a free field nor a conformal point, it provides an alternative, non-perturbative route to renormalization, internal to the quantum in- verse scattering method, which applies wherever an ultralocal lattice regularization is available, including asymptotically free sigma models.
♻ ☆ Gravitational Bremsstrahlung Waveform at the fourth Post-Minkowskian order and the second Post-Newtonian level
Donato Bini, Thibault Damour, Andrea Geralico
Using the Multipolar Post-Minkowskian formalism, we compute the frequency-domain waveform generated by the gravitational scattering of two nonspinning bodies at the fourth post-Minkowskian order ($O(G^4)$, or two-loop order), and at the fractional second Post-Newtonian accuracy ($O(v^4/c^4)$). The waveform is decomposed in spin-weighted spherical harmonics and the needed radiative multipoles, $U_{\ell m}(ω), V_{\ell m}(ω)$, are explicitly expressed in terms of a small number of master integrals. The basis of master integrals contains both (modified) Bessel functions, and solutions of inhomogeneous Bessel equations with Bessel-function sources. We show how to express the latter in terms of Meijer G functions. The low-frequency expansion of our results is checked againg existing classical soft theorems. We also complete our previous results on the $O(G^2)$ bremsstrahlung waveform by computing the $O(G^3)$ spectral densities of radiated energy and momentum, in the rest frame of one body, at the thirtieth order in velocity.

♻ ☆ Analytic Spread Complexity from Level Statistics: From Chaos to Integrability
Pallab Basu, Suman das, Bigboy Madlala
Spread complexity has emerged as a useful probe of quantum chaos, yet the microscopic spectral origin of its characteristic finite-time peak remains incompletely understood. We develop an analytic framework that relates spread complexity directly to local spectral statistics. Starting from an energy-space representation of the Krylov kernel, we show that the kernel is approximately banded, leading to a rapidly convergent diagonal expansion dominated by nearby levels in the ordered spectrum. Motivated by this structure, we propose an approximate kernel-universality hypothesis: after unfolding, the Krylov kernel is well approximated by that of a uniform lattice. Combining this universal kernel with local spectral statistics yields a simple analytic expression for spread complexity in terms of the Fourier transforms of the $k$-th nearest-neighbour spacing distributions. In particular, at leading order, the finite-time peak is controlled by the Fourier transform of the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution. The resulting framework describes both chaotic random-matrix ensembles and the integrable Poisson limit, identifies the spectral origin of the complexity peak and its late-time behaviour, and provides a direct connection between Krylov dynamics and spectral statistics.
comment: A new appendix and a few comments have been added
♻ ☆ Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
Yuxuan Guo
We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb Z_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern--Simons--Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf8_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf8_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

♻ ☆ Accelerating systems as probes of Lorentz violation
Quentin G. Bailey, Nils A. Nilsson, Sawyer J. Star
We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for Lorentz violation. The dispersion relation, Hamiltonian, and massless and massive Wightman functions are obtained. We determine the conditions under which the scalar dynamics preserves boost symmetry and distinguish these from the weaker conditions required for stationarity along a single accelerated worldline. The Wightman functions are used to construct the finite-time Unruh-DeWitt response for a uniformly accelerated detector. For generic coefficients the response is nonstationary and depends on both the duration and temporal location of the measurement. The spectrum, which is the resulting excitation rate as a function of the energy level difference in the detector, is obtained numerically. It shows discernable differences with the usual massive thermal spectrum for dimensionless coefficients on the order of $10^{-7}$. Experimental implications of the result are discussed. As an alternative viewpoint, we place Lorentz violation in the point-particle sector, derive the exact trajectory generated by a constant electric field, and study the proper-time Fourier response of a conventional scalar wave along the modified trajectory.
comment: 28 pages, 6 figures. Explanation added and clarity improved. Accepted for publication in PRD
♻ ☆ Quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with nontrivial sound speed in inflation
Shi-Cheng Liu, Lei-Hua Liu, Bichu Li, Hai-Qing Zhang, Peng-Zhang He
In this work, we systematically investigate the quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with a nontrivial sound speed, utilizing a normalized open two-mode squeezed-state framework. Rather than introducing new observables, our analysis focuses on how a modified sound speed dynamically reshapes the Schrödinger evolution of the squeezing parameters ($r_k$ and $φ_k$). We demonstrate how these dynamical changes are inherited by the reduced density matrix of the observable sector. By employing a sound-speed-resonance parametrization, we derive and evaluate the purity, von Neumann entropy, Rényi entropies, and logarithmic negativity. We introduce a bounded variable $x = \tanh r_k$ and perform numerical simulations within the inflationary regime. Our numerical results reveal that a nontrivial sound speed significantly suppresses the purity of the reduced state, indicating enhanced effective mixedness. Simultaneously, it strongly amplifies and modulates both the entropic and entanglement diagnostics. More precisely, a nontrivial sound speed postpones the onset of classicality by modulating the decoherence process. Ultimately, we show that a nontrivial sound speed leaves distinct and identifiable quantum-information signatures within the entanglement structure of the early universe.

♻ ☆ New RG flows between non-Unitary CFTs from exact massless scattering theories
Changrim Ahn, Zoltan Bajnok, Soma Elek
We construct complete solutions of the massless S-matrix bootstrap equations describing a new infinite family of integrable RG flows from the higher-fusion-level minimal models M(3,2n+3;n) to the non-unitary Virasoro minimal models M(2,2n+3), including a flow from M(3,5) to the Yang--Lee CFT M(2,5) when n=1. We provide strong evidence for this identification by matching conformal perturbation theory around the UV fixed points with the small-volume expansion of the corresponding thermodynamic Bethe ansatz equations. We further show that a family of non-invertible Verlinde defect lines is preserved along the flows.

♻ ☆ Holomorphic Floer theory I: exponential integrals in finite and infinite dimensions
Maxim Kontsevich, Yan Soibelman
In the first of the series of papers devoted to our project ``Holomorphic Floer Theory" we discuss exponential integrals and related wall-crossing structures. We emphasize two points of view on the subject: the one based on the ideas of deformation quantization and the one based on the ideas of Floer theory. Their equivalence is a corollary of our generalized Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. In the case of exponential integrals this amounts to several comparison isomorphisms between local and global versions of de Rham and Betti cohomology. We develop the corresponding theories in particular generalizing Morse-Novikov theory to the holomorphic case. We prove that arising wall-crossing structures are analytic. As a corollary, perturbative expansions of exponential integrals are resurgent. Based on a careful study of finite-dimensional exponential integrals we propose a conjectural approach to infinite-dimensional exponential integrals. We illustrate this approach in the case of Feynman path integral with holomorphic Lagrangian boundary conditions as well as in the case of the complexified Chern-Simons theory. We discuss the arising perverse sheaf of infinite rank as well as analyticity of the corresponding ``Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure". We develop a general theory of quantum wave functions and show that in the case of Chern-Simons theory it gives an alternative description of the Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure based on the notion of generalized Nahm sum. We propose several conjectures about analyticity and resurgence of the corresponding perturbative series.

The status of several representative gauge theories on various quantum space-times, mainly focusing on Yang-Mills type extensions together with a few matrix model formulations is overviewed. The common building blocks are derivation based differential calculus possibly twisted and noncommutative analog of the Koszul connection. The star-products related to the quantum space-times are obtained from a combination of harmonic analysis of group algebras combined with Weyl quantization. The remaining problems inherent to gauge theories on Moyal spaces in their two different formulations are outlined. A family of gauge invariant matrix models on $\mathbb{R}^3_λ$, a deformation of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is presented among which a solvable model. The characterization of 11 new quantum Minkowski space-times through their $*$-algebras is given. A gauge theory of Yang-Mills type is constructed on one recently explored of these space-times and compared to its counterpart built on the popular $κ$-Minkowski.

♻ ☆ A strongly hyperbolic viscous relativistic hydrodynamics theory with first-order charge current
Federico Schianchi, Fernando Abalos
We extend the first order dissipative relativistic hydrodynamics model of Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha- Kovtun (BDNK) in order to include the charge number current in full first order expansion with out-of-equilibrium contribution proportional to the evolution equation of the ideal fluid. We obtain a fully second order system of partial differential equation (PDE) that can be casted in a fully conservative way. We analyze the hyperbolicity of this model coupled to Einstein field equations using a newly developed technique that allows for hyperbolicity studies without explicit first order reduction. Furthermore, we identify a frame choice where our formulation is causal, stable and with positive entropy generation for a wide range of equations of state (EoS). Our analysis shows that the inclusion of an out-of-equilibrium correction to the charge current, plays an important role in guaranteeing the strong hyperbolicity and, therefore, the well-posedness of the system.

♻ ☆ Dressed Subsystems in Classical Gravity
Pranav Pulakkat
This paper considers the problem of consistently defining subsystems in gravitational theories. It is argued that a subsystem is a spacetime subregion in which the observables form a closed Poisson algebra. In a generally covariant theory, the location of the subregion must be determined in relation to other degrees of freedom. It is proposed that these degrees of freedom should live within the region, so that an observer can determine its edge by only measuring fields inside of it. This turns out to be equivalent to the property that observables in the subregion generate field-dependent gauge transformations on the causal complement. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that this is \textit{exactly} what is necessary for the observables to form a Poisson algebra and thus to constitute a consistent subsystem. Observables in spacelike separated "dressed subsystems" are shown to commute. Several examples are given in the context of General Relativity. Along the way, new perspectives on the covariant phase space formalism are introduced that clarify well-known issues, such as the factorization of subregions in gauge theories and the unambiguous definition of Noether charges associated with one-sided boosts. Finally, prospects for extending these results to a perturbative quantum setting are discussed.
comment: 53 pages, figures. Revised to clarify technical details of assumptions
♻ ☆ Virasoro Symmetry in Neural Network Field Theories
Brandon Robinson
We construct the Virasoro algebra from a neural free-field architecture. A logarithmic momentum law and a smooth spectral window give the weight-one current kernel, whose radial-ordering discontinuity fixes the oscillator pairing. The limiting neural current correlations agree with the Fock vacuum correlations. Their Sugawara stress tensor gives the Virasoro algebra with central charge one, and charged vertex insertions identify its highest-weight sectors. Bounds on regulator and feature errors control finite-mode approximations to this representation. At finite width, an explicit adjoint-compatible projection defines an auxiliary Fock readout when its Hermitian mixed block is positive. Cauchy features extend the construction to fermionic and supersymmetric sectors, including a Clifford zero mode in the Ramond representation, while first-order stress tensors give fermionic and bosonic ghost systems. Shared reflected features impose scalar boundary conditions in every realization and yield conformal and superconformal gluing in the limiting fields. Numerical comparisons support the current pairing and field correlations; their detailed analysis is collected in the appendices.
comment: 1+49 pages, 8 figures, 1 table; v4: expanded analytic construction and finite-width analysis; clarified Fock admissibility; added Ward checks; updated figures and references; corrected typos
♻ ☆ Neutron stars in $f(Q) = Q +ξQ^2$ gravity
J. C. N. de Araujo, H. G. M. Fortes
Modified theories of gravity based on the symmetric teleparallel framework have recently attracted considerable attention as viable alternatives to General Relativity. In this context, f(Q) gravity, in which the gravitational interaction is encoded in the nonmetricity scalar Q, provides a consistent geometrical formulation that differs from the standard curvature-based description. In this work, we investigate the structure of neutron stars within a family of f(Q) gravity models by employing realistic equations of state, namely FPS, SLy, ENG and MPA1. Using the covariant formulation of f(Q) gravity, we derive the corresponding Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and apply them to model compact stellar configurations. Numerical integration of the field equations provides the mass-radius relations and the maximum masses supported by each equation of state, enabling a direct comparison with current observational constraints. Furthermore, we analyze the behavior of the nonmetricity scalar both inside and outside the stellar object, providing additional insight into the gravitational structure of compact stars in this framework.

☆ Prediction and Screening of $η$-carbide-type Nitrides for Ammonia Synthesis
Luka H. Mikek, Nicholas D. Humphrey, Andrea Ambrosini, Matthew D. Witman, Dallas R. Trinkle
Synthesis of ammonia is of critical importance to applications in energy, industrial chemistry, and especially agriculture, and is accomplished industrially using the carbon- and energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. η-carbide-type nitrides such as Co3Mo3N have gained attention in recent years as alternative ammonia synthesis catalysts with the potential to lower these energy demands. Co3Mo3N is experimentally observed to undergo a reversible phase transition from Co3Mo3N to Co6Mo6N, offering a chemical looping-based NH3 synthesis route that has not been fully explored. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

Angel Rodríguez-Fernández, Jan-Etienne Pudell, Roman Shayduk, Alejandro Fraile-Gimeno, Wonhyuk Jo, James Wrigley, Johannes Möller, Alexey Zozulya, Jörg Hallmann, Anders Madsen, Pablo Villanueva-Perez, Zdenek Matej, Thies J. Albert, Dominik Kaczmarek, Klaus Sokolowski-Tinten, Antonowicz Jerzy, Ryszard Sobierajski, Rahimi Mosafer, Oleksii I. Liubchenko, Javier Solis, Jan Siegel
Material processing with femtosecond lasers has attracted enormous attention because of its potential for technology and industrial applications. In parallel, time-resolved x-ray diffraction has been successfully used to study ultrafast structural distortion dynamics in semiconductor thin films or surface layers. However, real-world processing applications mostly are concerned with bulk materials, which prevents the use of x-ray surface based techniques. For processing applications, a fast and depth-sensitive probe is needed. To address this, we present a novel technique based on ultrafast x-ray dynamical diffraction (UDD) capable of imaging transient strain distributions inside bulk crystals upon laser excitation. This pump-probe technique provides a complete picture of thetemporal evolution of ultrafast distorted lattice depth profiles. We demonstrate the potential of UDD by studying a thin Si single crystal upon single pulse femtosecond optical excitation. Our study reveals that below the melting threshold strong lattice distortions not only longitudinal, but also transversal to the propagation of the strain wave appear on picosecond time scales along the single crystal. The observation of this transversal deformation after laser excitation contradicts previous work that were not able to observed it, what could be related to the high sensitivity of dynamical diffraction with respect to the lattice distortions. The speed of propagation of this ultrafast transversal strain deformation is observed to be slower to the longitudinal sound speed for Si as described in the bibliography.
♻ ☆ Spin disorder competing with positional symmetry breaking governs the metal-insulator behavior in oxide paramagnets
Jia-Xin Xiong, Xiuwen Zhang, Alex Zunger
Numerous transition-metal oxides have low-temperature, long-range-ordered antiferromagnetic (AFM) states that are generally insulating, and high-temperature, disordered paramagnetic (PM) phases. The latter can be either insulating (predicted here for NaFeO3), or metallic (predicted here and previously observed in NaOsO3). Similar distinctions have been traditionally affected in strongly correlated models by the value used for Coulomb repulsion U. Here we show an alternative, strong-correlation-free (U=0) view suggesting that the distinction between insulating and metallic PM phases is governed by the competition between local magnetic moment disorder and the polymorphous distribution of off-center atomic displacements. Such parameter-free, energy-lowering symmetry breaking density functional calculations provide a framework for understanding metal-insulator behaviors across different quantum materials in terms of measurable local structural and magnetic parameters.

♻ ☆ Strain-induced splitting of the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition in 1T-TaS$_2$
M. M. Tyumentsev, V. E. Minakova, N. I. Fedotov, S. V. Zaitsev-Zotov
The effects of uniaxial and biaxial tensile strain on the $ρ_{xx}$ and $ρ_{yy}$ components of the resistivity tensor and the commensurate --- nearly commensurate CDW (CCDW-NCCDW) transition temperature in 1T-TaS$_2$ are studied. At room temperature, uniaxial tensile strain increases the resistivity tensor components by a comparable magnitude both parallel and perpendicular to the strain axis. In the case of biaxial strain, up to 20~K decrease in the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperature is observed. In the case of uniaxial strain, a new phase with two different CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperatures is observed, the splitting exceeds 10 K. The occurrence of such a phase is associated with the transition of the CDW into the commensurate state along the tensile strain direction while maintaining nearly commensurability along the perpendicular one. The results allow to justify various models widely used in analysis of transport properties of 1T-TaS$_2$ in commensurate and nearly commensurate states.

♻ ☆ Multi-Species Multi-Reaction Model Parametrization of a Commercial NCA Positive Electrode from Half-Cell Open-Circuit Potential Data
Michele Galasso, Petr Čech, Ivo Horstkötter, Simon Schwunk, Zuzana Vlčková Živcová, Václav Knap
Physics-based models of lithium-ion batteries require the open-circuit potential (OCP) of each electrode as a function of its lithiation. The multi-species multi-reaction (MSMR) model provides a compact, thermodynamically grounded description of this relationship, representing each insertion reaction by a standard potential, a site fraction and a disorder parameter. Here, we parametrize the MSMR model for nickel-cobalt-aluminum oxide (NCA), a cathode chemistry widespread in automotive cells, using the positive electrode of a commercial silicon-graphite/NCA cell. Cathode material was harvested from a pristine cell and from cells cycle-aged to the end of life under two state-of-charge windows, and its half-cell OCP was measured by slow galvanostatic cycling. Smooth differential-capacity curves were obtained by histogram counting, and the charge and discharge branches were fitted with a constrained, scale-invariant optimization that keeps every reaction anchored to a visible peak. We report the first MSMR parameter set for an NCA cathode and show, through a differential-capacity peak analysis across aging states, that its thermodynamic signature is essentially unchanged by aging. This finding supports the common modeling practice of holding the electrode's intrinsic parameters fixed and ascribing aging to electrode-level capacity and alignment changes.

♻ ☆ Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction NeurIPS 2026
Aamod Varma, Shuyi Jia, Victor Fung
Diffusion-based pretraining has emerged as a powerful strategy for learning transferable representations in graph neural networks for materials property prediction without requiring quantum-mechanical labels such as energies, forces, and stresses for every pretraining structure. However, the method retains a critical dependency: it requires structures residing near local minima of a potential energy surface, which have traditionally been obtained through costly DFT relaxations of known or physically synthesized compounds. This reliance constrains both the scale and the structural diversity of available pretraining data, leaving large regions of crystal structure space unexplored. In this work, we connect diffusion-based pretraining with synthetic structure generation to reduce this bottleneck. We introduce a synthetic data generation pipeline combining three complementary strategies: perturb-and-relax, generative sampling via MatterGen, and protostructure enumeration. Where structural relaxation is required, we use fast machine-learned interatomic potentials instead of performing a new DFT relaxation for each generated structure. We further compare a coordinate-denoising control with continuous-time variance-preserving (VP) and sub-VP diffusion objectives using a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone. The source comparison covers seven MatBench property-prediction tasks, and an eighth task, \texttt{mp\_gap}, is included in the protostructure scaling study. Every synthetic-pretraining condition numerically outperforms random initialization on all seven source-comparison tasks. Scaling the protostructure corpus from 20k to 165k under a fixed 400-epoch schedule numerically matches or exceeds MP-20k pretraining on most tasks; because this protocol increases both data diversity and optimization updates, the result reflects joint data-and-compute scaling.
comment: 14 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Accepted at the AI4Mat Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
♻ ☆ Defect-limited thermal transport in AlN using pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials
Minseok Moon, Wonjun Choi, Seungwu Han, Youngho Kang
Aluminum nitride (AlN) is an important thermal management material whose high lattice thermal conductivity is strongly suppressed by oxygen impurities. We investigate phonon scattering by oxygen-related defects using pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), molecular dynamics (MD), and phonon Boltzmann transport calculations. Several pretrained MLIPs are benchmarked against density functional theory for phonon dispersions and pristine thermal conductivity. To balance accuracy and computational speed, we use a fine-tuned version of the compact SevenNet-Nano model for MD simulations. Monte Carlo annealing supports the formation of bound $V_{\mathrm{Al}}(\mathrm{O_N})_3$ complexes, whose scattering differs from that of their isolated constituents. Defect scattering rates extracted from excess spectral energy density (SED) linewidths agree reasonably with harmonic $T$-matrix predictions at low oxygen contents, supporting the independent-scatterer approximation. Incorporating these rates into an iterative Boltzmann transport equation with Bose--Einstein statistics yields thermal conductivities comparable to experimental values and captures their observed decrease with oxygen content. At high concentrations, however, the scattering rate deviates from linear scaling with oxygen content, suggesting limitations of independent-defect and pristine-phonon descriptions. These results demonstrate an efficient approach using pretrained MLIPs to quantify defect-limited thermal transport and provide insights into impurity effects beyond the dilute-defect approximation.

♻ ☆ How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
Jiho Lee, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han, Jung-Hoon Lee, Jisu Jung, Youngho Kang, Sungwoo Kang
Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.

♻ ☆ Symmetry-Enabled Ferroelectric Valley Transduction in Rhombohedral Bilayer WSe$_2$
Katsunori Wakabayashi, Souren Adhikary, Tomoaki Kameda, Kazuhito Tsukagoshi
Ferroelectric polarization couples to the layer degree of freedom in a bilayer, but a valley-selective energy response requires the valleys to carry different interlayer character. Rhombohedral bilayer WSe$_2$ meets that condition by symmetry: three-fold rotation forbids interlayer tunneling at the $K$ valley, while strong hybridization remains at $Γ$. The resulting contrast converts the band-effective ferroelectric layer asymmetry into a shift of the $K$ edge, and so displaces the $K$--$Γ$ landscape: a finite-field fit that does not impose the rule leaves the $K$ coupling consistent with zero, and the shift reaches 41.7 meV, the most that asymmetry can give a single valley. Reversing the polarization mirrors the valley landscape in displacement field, so the two registries have equal and opposite differential transconductance $g_d$ at zero field. In the ideal symmetric limit a second parity holds about each registry's own compensation field and places a zero of $g_d$ there. The valley-dependent screening calculated here displaces that zero by only 0.2 % at the read point, so device asymmetry limits the accuracy. The result links a known stacking selection rule to ferroelectric valley transduction, with a quantitative valley shift and a directly testable transport signature.

♻ ☆ The two-level systems in cryogenic solids, or how to avoid stressful memories
Vassiliy Lubchenko
Structural glasses prepared by bulk quenching a liquid melt universally exhibit puzzling low-energy excitations commonly known as the ``two-level systems'' (TLSs). Recent studies indicate that ultrastable glassy films made by vapor deposition exhibit substantially fewer TLSs and, at the same time, are more stable enthalpically than conventional glasses made by quenching a melt. A similar phenomenon is observed in very stable glasses of model liquid mixtures prepared using swap Monte Carlo sampling. However, in a separate set of enthalpically stable solids, exemplified by amber matured over geological times, the two-level systems persist. In addressing this seeming conflict, we emphasize that a depletion of the TLSs, if any, means the configurational entropy of the material is lower than that of conventional glasses made by bulk-quenching a melt. Ageing does induce reduction in configurational entropy, but amber, we speculate, achieves enthalpic stabilization through increased bonding, not ageing. We separately comment on the discrepancy among existing predictions for the extent of cooperativity of the two-level systems. Several experiments are suggested to test the present picture.
♻ ☆ Drying-induced film formation in redispersible polymer powder: a time-resolved mechanical study
Justine Henry, Sébastien Manneville, Ludovic Feige, Clara Paillard, Thibaut Divoux
The mechanical evolution of latex dispersions during drying remains poorly understood, despite its importance for coatings, adhesives, and construction materials. Here, we use time-resolved mechanical spectroscopy to follow the formation of a polymer film from a dense aqueous latex suspension. The viscoelastic spectra retain a power-law frequency dependence and collapse onto a master curve using time-dependent shift factors, revealing a time-aging superposition principle. Moreover, the frequency shift factor eventually plateaus, suggesting a crossover toward arrested particle dynamics and film formation. This scenario is robustly observed at various temperatures, allowing us to determine an apparent activation energy associated with film formation. Finally, the non-linear response of the dispersion, measured throughout film formation, shows a ductile-to-brittle transition, consistent with the emergence of a solid-like film. Together, these results establish a rheological picture of the transformation from a dense colloidal suspension into a continuous polymer film.

♻ ☆ A Resolution to the Marcus-Rehm-Weller Paradox in Electron Transfer
Ethan Abraham
Marcus theory famously predicts that electron-transfer rates decrease once the thermodynamic driving force exceeds the reorganization energy. Yet many systems instead exhibit Rehm-Weller kinetics, characterized by rate saturation rather than decrease. Here we show that these apparently contradictory phenomenologies can emerge as opposite physical limits of the same two-state harmonic Hamiltonian. In the normal region, the model recovers both Marcus and Rehm-Weller behavior. In the inverted region, however, it predicts Marcus's decreasing rate in the nonadiabatic limit but Rehm-Weller saturation in the adiabatic limit. Using physically plausible reorganization energies and electronic coupling values, we show that Rehm-Weller's data can be quantitatively reproduced within a microscopic quantum model. Finally, we note that the model predicts three regions of adiabatic electron transfer: (1) a normal region with kinetics governed by an effective reorganization energy, (2) a finite region of barrierless transfer, and (3) a region in which the correspondence between diabatic and adiabatic states is reversed, suppressing the Marcus rate.
♻ ☆ Assessing the Transferability of General-Purpose MachineLearning Interatomic Potentials for Heterogeneous Catalysis with HetCat26
Alexandre Peuch, Angus Whiteside, Giaan Kler-Young, Kaifeng Niu, Jinwoo Hwang, Manos Mavrikakis, Angelos Michaelides, Fabian Berger
Foundation machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise near-density functional theory (DFT) accuracy across broad areas of chemistry and materials science. However, their performance in describing systems and processes relevant to heterogeneous catalysis remains underexplored. Here, we introduce HetCat26, a collection of benchmark tests designed to assess pre-trained MLIPs across key aspects of catalytic modeling, including surface energetics, metal-metal oxide interactions, adsorption, and catalytic reaction networks. Evaluating eighteen foundation models, we find that performance on existing general materials benchmarks is only weakly predictive of performance on HetCat26; transferability to heterogeneous catalysis cannot be inferred from these general benchmarks. Across the benchmark tests, current models describe surface energetics and, perhaps surprisingly, reaction barriers well, whereas larger errors are observed for adsorption, and DFT site preferences are often not reproduced. Three models, eSEN-30M-OAM, SevenNet-Omni-i12 and MACE-MH-1-OMAT, nevertheless achieve high accuracy across the properties evaluated. Beyond model benchmarking, HetCat26 highlights the importance of training data consistency: PBE and PBE+U calculations should not be mixed within a training set. Overall, we identify challenges limiting the transferability of current foundation MLIPs to heterogeneous catalysis and, more broadly, to chemical reactions at interfaces, providing guidance for the development of the next generation of foundation models.
♻ ☆ Emergence and Detection of Surface altermagnetism in KV$_2$Se$_2$O
Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Colin Lange, Sergio Rodríguez Fernández, Atasi Chakraborty, Alexander Mook, Jairo Sinova
We demonstrate the recent concept of emergent surface altermagnetism through its unique signatures in KV$_2$Se$_2$O. We show that for bulk antiferromagnetically ordered KV$_2$Se$_2$O, the (001) surface exhibits $d$-wave altermagnetism. Our results fully explain the recent seemingly contradicgting experimental evidence, independently showing both an antiferromagnetically ordered bulk from neutron diffraction, and $d$-wave spin splitting from photoemission spectroscopy. To fully verify this conecept, we predict, as a key experimental signature, a large nonlinear Edelstein response, which is localized at the surface, and follows the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry. These results are not only relevant for the metallic and room-temperature magnet KV$_2$Se$_2$O, but also for several other Lieb lattice systems. Our work expands the pool of techniques that can be used to detect altermagnetism emerging at the surfaces of antiferromagnets.

☆ Exact Parent Hamiltonians for Partially Magnetized Chiral Spin Liquids
Xin Shen, Guangyue Ji, Jie Wang
Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing various bosonic topological orders. Our construction relies on an exact Hubbard-type parent Hamiltonian for bosonic lattice fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, valid at arbitrary repulsive interaction strengths. Taking the on-site repulsion to infinity and applying local boson-spin mappings yields exact parent Hamiltonians for the CSLs. Our two-spin construction generalizes the Kalmeyer-Laughlin spin Hamiltonian to a broader class of bosonic FQH model states, including Abelian states and non-Abelian parton states. We derive controlled microscopic realizations of these two-spin Hamiltonians via second-order superexchange in generalized spinful Hofstadter-Hubbard models with tailored hoppings and interactions. With more general local constraints and interactions, boson-spin mappings yield exact higher-spin and multispin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs.

☆ From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
David Valenzuela, Alfredo Raya
Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

☆ Computing $F$-Symbols from Modular Data
Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham
We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free. Although the algorithm is implemented numerically, we describe a reliable means of recovering the exact $F$-symbols, assuming that in some gauge they lie in a given number field, and of certifying every pentagon and hexagon equation exactly. The exotic rank-11 anisotropic modular category B11-00119 (https://anyonatlas.org/data/B11-00119), with largest fusion coefficient 4, is used as a motivating example, for which the solve takes roughly 10 minutes on a laptop. We will continue to add $F$-symbol solutions to https://AnyonAtlas.org as they are completed.

☆ Learning the Anyon Atlas
Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham, Zekai Zhu
We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion. We demonstrate the scalability of this gated implementation by identifying prime modular data at rank 100 that is not realized by any Chern-Simons theory. The identified data through rank 42 has been made available at https://AnyonAtlas.org, to which further data will be added as it is found.

☆ An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
Arun Debray, Weicheng Ye, Matthew Yu
We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(τ_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.
comment: 78 pages. Comments welcome!
☆ The magical memory cost of entanglement spectrum compression
Matias Karjula, Vilma Nieminen, Teemu Ojanen, Tapio Ala-Nissila, Moein N. Ivaki
How much quantum memory is needed to faithfully retain the entanglement spectrum of a bipartite pure state after separating out Bell pairs through local unitaries? We derive the exact tradeoff between Bell-pair yield, residual memory, and reconstruction fidelity under local unitaries, defining an operational measure of entanglement-spectrum complexity. Smoothed entanglement spread bounds this memory cost from below, while diverging nonlocal magic forces unbounded memory at any fixed positive fidelity. Chaotic circuit dynamics exhibit a transient memory peak whose height increases with system size, followed by declining cost despite continued entropy growth. A large typical Haar-random state requires only an accuracy-dependent memory, whereas stationary fermionic Gaussian states retain a growing cost with size. In the circuits studied, the multiscale spectral structure associated with entanglement catalysis also has a practical consequence for matrix product state compression, yielding a multiplicative overhead not captured by the conventional entropy-based bond dimension estimate.
☆ Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
Joshua Aftergood, Daniele Guerci, Jacob Brunton, Feng Zhang, Thomas Iadecola, Peter P. Orth, Cai-Zhuang Wang, Nicola Lanatà, Yong-Xin Yao
Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework, t-GQCE, for generic multi-orbital lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians. Within the time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation, the lattice dynamics is mapped onto a noninteracting quasiparticle lattice, propagated classically, coupled to finite interacting embedding models propagated on quantum processors. The two parts exchange only embedding Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices, and the framework is agnostic to the quantum dynamics solver. We demonstrate it with adaptive variational quantum dynamics simulations of interaction quenches in the Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. Without ghost orbitals, the embedding problem reduces to a single qubit, simulated on IBM quantum hardware with two qubits, including an ancilla. With more ghost orbitals, t-GQCE suppresses the artificial undamped oscillations of the conventional Gutzwiller approximation and approaches nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results for weak and strong quenches. Statevector simulations with 2, 4 and 6 ghost orbitals per spin, or 8, 12 and 16 qubits, give adaptive circuits that follow the embedding states with infidelities below $5\times10^{-4}$. Under trapped-ion noise models, circuit compression, measurements in rotated orbital bases with post-selection, and noise mitigation reduce the measurement errors severalfold. At one third of the error rates of a hardware-benchmarked noise model, they reach an accuracy of $0.01$ for the single-particle density matrix and the double occupancy with $10^5$ shots per time step, and the Quantinuum H2-Emulator gives similar accuracy.

☆ $1/N$ corrections to $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in QED$_3$, QED$_3$--GNY and scalar QED$_3$
Yongwei Guo, Zhijin Li, Ke Ren
Three-dimensional Abelian gauge theories have broad applications in deconfined quantum criticality, Dirac spin liquids and cuprate superconductivity. Correlation functions of conserved currents $J$ and the stress tensor $T$ carry fundamental information about these theories. We compute the first subleading large-flavor corrections to the parity-even three-point functions $\langle TJJ\rangle$ and $\langle TTT\rangle$ in QED$_3$, QED$_3$--Gross--Neveu--Yukawa, and critical scalar QED$_3$. For $\langle TJJ\rangle$, we study both global flavor currents and the topological $U(1)$ current, which measures the magnetic flux of the dynamical gauge field. We evaluate the flat-space energy flux in directions where the leading free-field profile vanishes. At first subleading order the flux in these directions is determined by four-particle production, yielding analytic corrections to the conformal collider parameters. We reproduce the corrections independently from squashed-sphere free-energy derivatives. Together with known two-point normalizations, the collider parameters fix the coefficients of both independent tensor structures in each correlator. Our results are useful for studying conductivity and shear response near quantum critical points and for conformal bootstrap studies of conserved-current and stress-tensor correlators in strongly coupled gauge theories.
comment: 36+22 pages, 8 figures
☆ Conformal defects in a quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain: an exactly parametrized Ising defect line and a relevant vacancy
R. L. Silva. R. C. Silva, A. R. Pereira
The quasi-one-dimensional Kitaev chain of coupled hexagonal plaquettes recently introduced by Majumder is exactly solvable in terms of free Majorana fermions and undergoes a topological transition at the exchange anisotropy $J_x=\sqrt{2}\,J$. By eliminating the two-coordinated sites of each plaquette we reduce the zero-energy problem to a uniform Majorana chain, which yields the critical point, a single Majorana cone at $k=0$ (hence an Ising critical point with central charge $c=\tfrac12$), and closed forms for every defect quantity that follows. A weakened inter-plaquette bond $λJ_x$ is an exactly marginal defect with transmission $T=4λ^2/(1+λ^2)^2$ at low energy, that is, $T=\sin^2 2φ$ with $\tanφ=λ$: the bond traverses the ferromagnetic defect line of the Ising conformal field theory from the transparent point to the cut chain, and we give its exact energy dependence on the lattice. The intra-plaquette bonds land on the same line with different parametrizations: a $y$ or $z$ bond has $\tanφ=(1+λ)/2$ and covers only $T\in[0.64,1]$, because the plaquette provides a parallel path, whereas an $x$ bond has $\tanφ=(1+λ)/2λ$ and covers the strong-link half of the line, $φ\in(π/4,π/2)$. The identification is closed by an independent observable: the coefficient of $\ln L$ in the entanglement entropy across the defect follows the conformal-field-theory function $σ(\sqrt T)/2$ of Brehm and Brunner to within $0.4\%$ along the whole line, with no adjustable parameter. A vacancy behaves in the opposite way. It never binds a plaquette flux, because plaquettes share no sites, but it leaves its singly bonded neighbor as a conserved classical spin whose dangling Majorana is a zero-energy resonance.
☆ Reconciling Models for Infinite-Layer Nickelate Superconductors: Role of Interstitial-$s$ Band or $A$-Pocket
Ao Zhang, Chao Deng, Leonard M. Verhoff, Mi Jiang, Run Yang, Zhixiang Shi, Karsten Held, Liang Si
Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), we compute and compare the strongly correlated electronic structures and optical spectra of various effective models for the infinite-layer nickelate LaNiO$_2$, ranging from a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ 1-band model to a full 6-band model with all Ni-$3d$ plus an interstitial-$s$ orbital. The results demonstrate that Ni-$3d$ 5-band models overestimate the Hundness picture, whereas 6-band models, which explicitly include the interstitial-$s$ band and have an $A$-pocket, recover the characteristic Mottness physics. Importantly, the influence of the interstitial-$s$ band on the correlations of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ band is negligible. Thus, superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates can be reliably described within a single-band Hubbard framework, while the accurate description of inter-orbital properties such as (optical) conductivities requires the inclusion of at least the interstitial-$s$ band.

☆ Non-Abelian Hall Effects of Flavor-Waves in $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ Skyrmions

Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.

We prove that the gap closing for continuous phase transitions can always be detected using the frequency-filtered gradient of the Hamiltonian. The gap-detecting measurement is gentle, so when the ground state is unique a single reusable copy of each reference ground state supports the full exploration (for degenerate ground states, polynomially many copies suffice). The quantum algorithm runs in polynomial time at inverse-polynomial gap resolution. We also give a classical algorithm that runs in quasipolynomial time at constant gap resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate how our algorithm accurately determines the phase structure of several model quantum systems.

Here we see that there can sometimes be a connection, but it is not typical. Again there is no general quantitative or qualitative connection. Each dynamical form of criticality behaves independently, though we do see that critical times tend to be of the same order of magnitude and give an argument for why this is the case. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.

By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.

Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4μ_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $μ_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,μ_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,μ_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.

The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments in quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and effective field theory.
